Gen.3.16.bsb: To the woman He said: “I will sharply increase your pain in childbirth; in pain you will bring forth children. Your desire will be for your husband, and he will rule over you.”
Gen.3.16.kjv: Unto the woman he said, I will greatly multiply thy sorrow and thy conception; in sorrow thou shalt bring forth children; and thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee.

Gen.1.26.bsb: Then God said, “Let Us make man in Our image, after Our likeness, to rule over the fish of the sea and the birds of the air, over the livestock, and over all the earth itself and every creature that crawls upon it.”
Gen.1.26.kjv: And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth.

Gen.1.27.bsb: So God created man in His own image; in the image of God He created him; male and female He created them.
Gen.1.27.kjv: So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them.

Gen.5.1.bsb: This is the book of the generations of Adam. In the day that God created man, He made him in His own likeness.
Gen.5.1.kjv: This is the book of the generations of Adam. In the day that God created man, in the likeness of God made he him;

Gen.9.6.bsb: Whoever sheds the blood of man, by man his blood will be shed; for in His own image God has made mankind.
Gen.9.6.kjv: Whoso sheddeth man’s blood, by man shall his blood be shed: for in the image of God made he man.

Gen.2.21.bsb: So the LORD God caused the man to fall into a deep sleep, and while he slept, He took one of the man’s ribs and closed up the area with flesh.
Gen.2.21.kjv: And the Lord God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam, and he slept: and he took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh instead thereof;

Gen.2.22.bsb: And from the rib that the LORD God had taken from the man, He made a woman and brought her to him.
Gen.2.22.kjv: And the rib, which the Lord God had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man.

Gen.2.18.bsb: The LORD God also said, “It is not good for the man to be alone. I will make for him a suitable helper.”
Gen.2.18.kjv: And the Lord God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him.

Gen.2.20.bsb: The man gave names to all the livestock, to the birds of the air, and to every beast of the field. But for Adam no suitable helper was found.
Gen.2.20.kjv: And Adam gave names to all cattle, and to the fowl of the air, and to every beast of the field; but for Adam there was not found an help meet for him.

Gen.2.23.bsb: And the man said: “This is now bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh; she shall be called ‘woman,’ for out of man she was taken.”
Gen.2.23.kjv: And Adam said, This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man.

Gen.2.24.bsb: For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be united to his wife, and they will become one flesh.
Gen.2.24.kjv: Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.

Gen.20.16.bsb: And he said to Sarah, “See, I am giving your brother a thousand pieces of silver. It is your vindication before all who are with you; you are completely cleared.”
Gen.20.16.kjv: And unto Sarah he said, Behold, I have given thy brother a thousand pieces of silver: behold, he is to thee a covering of the eyes, unto all that are with thee, and with all other: thus she was reproved.

Gen.24.64.bsb: And when Rebekah looked up and saw Isaac, she got down from her camel
Gen.24.64.kjv: And Rebekah lifted up her eyes, and when she saw Isaac, she lighted off the camel.

Gen.24.65.bsb: and asked the servant, “Who is that man in the field coming to meet us?” “It is my master,” the servant answered. So she took her veil and covered herself.
Gen.24.65.kjv: For she had said unto the servant, What man is this that walketh in the field to meet us? And the servant had said, It is my master: therefore she took a vail, and covered herself.

Gen.1.1.bsb: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.
Gen.1.1.kjv: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.

Gen.2.4.bsb: This is the account of the heavens and the earth when they were created, in the day that the LORD God made them.
Gen.2.4.kjv: These are the generations of the heavens and of the earth when they were created, in the day that the Lord God made the earth and the heavens,

Gen.2.5.bsb: Now no shrub of the field had yet appeared on the earth, nor had any plant of the field sprouted, for the LORD God had not yet sent rain upon the earth, and there was no man to cultivate the ground.
Gen.2.5.kjv: And every plant of the field before it was in the earth, and every herb of the field before it grew: for the Lord God had not caused it to rain upon the earth, and there was not a man to till the ground.

Gen.1.3.bsb: And God said, “Let there be light,” and there was light.
Gen.1.3.kjv: And God said, Let there be light: and there was light.

Gen.1.4.bsb: And God saw that the light was good, and He separated the light from the darkness.
Gen.1.4.kjv: And God saw the light, that it was good: and God divided the light from the darkness.

Gen.1.5.bsb: God called the light “day,” and the darkness He called “night.” And there was evening, and there was morning—the first day.
Gen.1.5.kjv: And God called the light Day, and the darkness he called Night. And the evening and the morning were the first day.

Gen.1.6.bsb: And God said, “Let there be an expanse between the waters, to separate the waters from the waters.”
Gen.1.6.kjv: And God said, Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters, and let it divide the waters from the waters.

Gen.1.7.bsb: So God made the expanse and separated the waters beneath it from the waters above. And it was so.
Gen.1.7.kjv: And God made the firmament, and divided the waters which were under the firmament from the waters which were above the firmament: and it was so.

Gen.1.8.bsb: God called the expanse “sky.” And there was evening, and there was morning—the second day.
Gen.1.8.kjv: And God called the firmament Heaven. And the evening and the morning were the second day.

Gen.1.9.bsb: And God said, “Let the waters under the sky be gathered into one place, so that the dry land may appear.” And it was so.
Gen.1.9.kjv: And God said, Let the waters under the heaven be gathered together unto one place, and let the dry land appear: and it was so.

Gen.1.10.bsb: God called the dry land “earth,” and the gathering of waters He called “seas.” And God saw that it was good.
Gen.1.10.kjv: And God called the dry land Earth; and the gathering together of the waters called he Seas: and God saw that it was good.

Gen.1.11.bsb: Then God said, “Let the earth bring forth vegetation: seed-bearing plants and fruit trees, each bearing fruit with seed according to its kind.” And it was so.
Gen.1.11.kjv: And God said, Let the earth bring forth grass, the herb yielding seed, and the fruit tree yielding fruit after his kind, whose seed is in itself, upon the earth: and it was so.

Gen.1.12.bsb: The earth produced vegetation: seed-bearing plants according to their kinds and trees bearing fruit with seed according to their kinds. And God saw that it was good.
Gen.1.12.kjv: And the earth brought forth grass, and herb yielding seed after his kind, and the tree yielding fruit, whose seed was in itself, after his kind: and God saw that it was good.

Gen.1.13.bsb: And there was evening, and there was morning—the third day.
Gen.1.13.kjv: And the evening and the morning were the third day.

Gen.1.14.bsb: And God said, “Let there be lights in the expanse of the sky to distinguish between the day and the night, and let them be signs to mark the seasons and days and years.
Gen.1.14.kjv: And God said, Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years:

Gen.1.15.bsb: And let them serve as lights in the expanse of the sky to shine upon the earth.” And it was so.
Gen.1.15.kjv: And let them be for lights in the firmament of the heaven to give light upon the earth: and it was so.

Gen.1.16.bsb: God made two great lights: the greater light to rule the day and the lesser light to rule the night. And He made the stars as well.
Gen.1.16.kjv: And God made two great lights; the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night: he made the stars also.

Gen.1.17.bsb: God set these lights in the expanse of the sky to shine upon the earth,
Gen.1.17.kjv: And God set them in the firmament of the heaven to give light upon the earth,

Gen.1.18.bsb: to preside over the day and the night, and to separate the light from the darkness. And God saw that it was good.
Gen.1.18.kjv: And to rule over the day and over the night, and to divide the light from the darkness: and God saw that it was good.

Gen.1.19.bsb: And there was evening, and there was morning—the fourth day.
Gen.1.19.kjv: And the evening and the morning were the fourth day.

Gen.1.20.bsb: And God said, “Let the waters teem with living creatures, and let birds fly above the earth in the open expanse of the sky.”
Gen.1.20.kjv: And God said, Let the waters bring forth abundantly the moving creature that hath life, and fowl that may fly above the earth in the open firmament of heaven.

Gen.1.21.bsb: So God created the great sea creatures and every living thing that moves, with which the waters teemed according to their kinds, and every winged bird after its kind. And God saw that it was good.
Gen.1.21.kjv: And God created great whales, and every living creature that moveth, which the waters brought forth abundantly, after their kind, and every winged fowl after his kind: and God saw that it was good.

Gen.1.22.bsb: Then God blessed them and said, “Be fruitful and multiply and fill the waters of the seas, and let birds multiply on the earth.”
Gen.1.22.kjv: And God blessed them, saying, Be fruitful, and multiply, and fill the waters in the seas, and let fowl multiply in the earth.

Gen.1.23.bsb: And there was evening, and there was morning—the fifth day.
Gen.1.23.kjv: And the evening and the morning were the fifth day.

Gen.1.24.bsb: And God said, “Let the earth bring forth living creatures according to their kinds: livestock, land crawlers, and beasts of the earth according to their kinds.” And it was so.
Gen.1.24.kjv: And God said, Let the earth bring forth the living creature after his kind, cattle, and creeping thing, and beast of the earth after his kind: and it was so.

Gen.1.28.bsb: God blessed them and said to them, “Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth and subdue it; rule over the fish of the sea and the birds of the air and every creature that crawls upon the earth.”
Gen.1.28.kjv: And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over every living thing that moveth upon the earth.

Gen.2.2.bsb: And by the seventh day God had finished the work He had been doing; so on that day He rested from all His work.
Gen.2.2.kjv: And on the seventh day God ended his work which he had made; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had made.

Gen.2.3.bsb: Then God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it, because on that day He rested from all the work of creation that He had accomplished.
Gen.2.3.kjv: And God blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it: because that in it he had rested from all his work which God created and made.

Gen.1.31.bsb: And God looked upon all that He had made, and indeed, it was very good. And there was evening, and there was morning—the sixth day.
Gen.1.31.kjv: And God saw every thing that he had made, and, behold, it was very good. And the evening and the morning were the sixth day.

Gen.3.6.bsb: When the woman saw that the tree was good for food and pleasing to the eyes, and that it was desirable for obtaining wisdom, she took the fruit and ate it. She also gave some to her husband who was with her, and he ate it.
Gen.3.6.kjv: And when the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was pleasant to the eyes, and a tree to be desired to make one wise, she took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, and gave also unto her husband with her; and he did eat.

Gen.3.11.bsb: “Who told you that you were naked?” asked the LORD God. “Have you eaten from the tree of which I commanded you not to eat?”
Gen.3.11.kjv: And he said, Who told thee that thou wast naked? Hast thou eaten of the tree, whereof I commanded thee that thou shouldest not eat?

Gen.3.12.bsb: And the man answered, “The woman whom You gave me, she gave me fruit from the tree, and I ate it.”
Gen.3.12.kjv: And the man said, The woman whom thou gavest to be with me, she gave me of the tree, and I did eat.

Gen.3.1.bsb: Now the serpent was more crafty than any beast of the field that the LORD God had made. And he said to the woman, “Did God really say, ‘You must not eat from any tree in the garden?’”
Gen.3.1.kjv: Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field which the Lord God had made. And he said unto the woman, Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?

Gen.3.2.bsb: The woman answered the serpent, “We may eat the fruit of the trees of the garden,
Gen.3.2.kjv: And the woman said unto the serpent, We may eat of the fruit of the trees of the garden:

Gen.3.3.bsb: but about the fruit of the tree in the middle of the garden, God has said, ‘You must not eat of it or touch it, or you will die.’”
Gen.3.3.kjv: But of the fruit of the tree which is in the midst of the garden, God hath said, Ye shall not eat of it, neither shall ye touch it, lest ye die.

Gen.3.4.bsb: “You will not surely die,” the serpent told the woman.
Gen.3.4.kjv: And the serpent said unto the woman, Ye shall not surely die:

Gen.3.5.bsb: “For God knows that in the day you eat of it, your eyes will be opened and you will be like God, knowing good and evil.”
Gen.3.5.kjv: For God doth know that in the day ye eat thereof, then your eyes shall be opened, and ye shall be as gods, knowing good and evil.

Gen.5.3.bsb: When Adam was 130 years old, he had a son in his own likeness, after his own image; and he named him Seth.
Gen.5.3.kjv: And Adam lived an hundred and thirty years, and begat a son in his own likeness, after his image; and called his name Seth:

Gen.6.5.bsb: Then the LORD saw that the wickedness of man was great upon the earth, and that every inclination of the thoughts of his heart was altogether evil all the time.
Gen.6.5.kjv: And God saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually.

Gen.8.21.bsb: When the LORD smelled the pleasing aroma, He said in His heart, “Never again will I curse the ground because of man, even though every inclination of his heart is evil from his youth. And never again will I destroy all living creatures as I have done.
Gen.8.21.kjv: And the Lord smelled a sweet savour; and the Lord said in his heart, I will not again curse the ground any more for man’s sake; for the imagination of man’s heart is evil from his youth; neither will I again smite any more every thing living, as I have done.

Gen.6.12.bsb: And God looked upon the earth and saw that it was corrupt; for all living creatures on the earth had corrupted their ways.
Gen.6.12.kjv: And God looked upon the earth, and, behold, it was corrupt; for all flesh had corrupted his way upon the earth.

Gen.3.8.bsb: Then the man and his wife heard the voice of the LORD God walking in the garden in the breeze of the day, and they hid themselves from the presence of the LORD God among the trees of the garden.
Gen.3.8.kjv: And they heard the voice of the Lord God walking in the garden in the cool of the day: and Adam and his wife hid themselves from the presence of the Lord God amongst the trees of the garden.

Gen.3.7.bsb: And the eyes of both of them were opened, and they knew that they were naked; so they sewed together fig leaves and made coverings for themselves.
Gen.3.7.kjv: And the eyes of them both were opened, and they knew that they were naked; and they sewed fig leaves together, and made themselves aprons.

Gen.3.10.bsb: “I heard Your voice in the garden,” he replied, “and I was afraid because I was naked; so I hid myself.”
Gen.3.10.kjv: And he said, I heard thy voice in the garden, and I was afraid, because I was naked; and I hid myself.

Gen.3.24.bsb: So He drove out the man and stationed cherubim on the east side of the Garden of Eden, along with a whirling sword of flame to guard the way to the tree of life.
Gen.3.24.kjv: So he drove out the man; and he placed at the east of the garden of Eden Cherubims, and a flaming sword which turned every way, to keep the way of the tree of life.

Gen.3.19.bsb: By the sweat of your brow you will eat your bread, until you return to the ground—because out of it were you taken. For dust you are, and to dust you shall return.”
Gen.3.19.kjv: In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.

Gen.3.15.bsb: And I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and her seed. He will crush your head, and you will strike his heel.”
Gen.3.15.kjv: And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.

Gen.49.26.bsb: The blessings of your father have surpassed the blessings of the ancient mountains and the bounty of the everlasting hills. May they rest on the head of Joseph, on the brow of the prince of his brothers.
Gen.49.26.kjv: The blessings of thy father have prevailed above the blessings of my progenitors unto the utmost bound of the everlasting hills: they shall be on the head of Joseph, and on the crown of the head of him that was separate from his brethren.

Gen.48.12.bsb: Then Joseph removed his sons from his father’s knees and bowed facedown.
Gen.48.12.kjv: And Joseph brought them out from between his knees, and he bowed himself with his face to the earth.

Gen.24.26.bsb: Then the man bowed down and worshiped the LORD,
Gen.24.26.kjv: And the man bowed down his head, and worshipped the Lord.

Gen.43.23.bsb: “It is fine,” said the steward. “Do not be afraid. Your God, the God of your father, gave you the treasure that was in your sacks. I received your silver.” Then he brought Simeon out to them.
Gen.43.23.kjv: And he said, Peace be to you, fear not: your God, and the God of your father, hath given you treasure in your sacks: I had your money. And he brought Simeon out unto them.

Gen.40.13.bsb: Within three days Pharaoh will lift up your head and restore your position. You will put Pharaoh’s cup in his hand, just as you did when you were his cupbearer.
Gen.40.13.kjv: Yet within three days shall Pharaoh lift up thine head, and restore thee unto thy place: and thou shalt deliver Pharaoh’s cup into his hand, after the former manner when thou wast his butler.

Gen.22.18.bsb: And through your offspring all nations of the earth will be blessed, because you have obeyed My voice.”
Gen.22.18.kjv: And in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed; because thou hast obeyed my voice.

Gen.31.4.bsb: So Jacob sent word and called Rachel and Leah to the field where his flocks were,
Gen.31.4.kjv: And Jacob sent and called Rachel and Leah to the field unto his flock,

Gen.31.5.bsb: and he told them, “I can see from your father’s countenance that his attitude toward me has changed; but the God of my father has been with me.
Gen.31.5.kjv: And said unto them, I see your father’s countenance, that it is not toward me as before; but the God of my father hath been with me.

Gen.31.6.bsb: You know that I have served your father with all my strength.
Gen.31.6.kjv: And ye know that with all my power I have served your father.

Gen.31.7.bsb: And although he has cheated me and changed my wages ten times, God has not allowed him to harm me.
Gen.31.7.kjv: And your father hath deceived me, and changed my wages ten times; but God suffered him not to hurt me.

Gen.24.67.bsb: And Isaac brought her into the tent of his mother Sarah and took Rebekah as his wife. And Isaac loved her and was comforted after his mother’s death.
Gen.24.67.kjv: And Isaac brought her into his mother Sarah’s tent, and took Rebekah, and she became his wife; and he loved her: and Isaac was comforted after his mother’s death.

Gen.45.15.bsb: Joseph kissed each of his brothers as he wept over them. And afterward his brothers talked with him.
Gen.45.15.kjv: Moreover he kissed all his brethren, and wept upon them: and after that his brethren talked with him.

Gen.2.7.bsb: Then the LORD God formed man from the dust of the ground and breathed the breath of life into his nostrils, and the man became a living being.
Gen.2.7.kjv: And the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.

Gen.5.2.bsb: Male and female He created them, and He blessed them. And in the day they were created, He called them “man.”
Gen.5.2.kjv: Male and female created he them; and blessed them, and called their name Adam, in the day when they were created.

Gen.2.16.bsb: And the LORD God commanded him, “You may eat freely from every tree of the garden,
Gen.2.16.kjv: And the Lord God commanded the man, saying, Of every tree of the garden thou mayest freely eat:

Gen.2.17.bsb: but you must not eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil; for in the day that you eat of it, you will surely die.”
Gen.2.17.kjv: But of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat of it: for in the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die.

Gen.2.15.bsb: Then the LORD God took the man and placed him in the Garden of Eden to cultivate and keep it.
Gen.2.15.kjv: And the Lord God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to dress it and to keep it.

Gen.1.29.bsb: Then God said, “Behold, I have given you every seed-bearing plant on the face of all the earth, and every tree whose fruit contains seed. They will be yours for food.
Gen.1.29.kjv: And God said, Behold, I have given you every herb bearing seed, which is upon the face of all the earth, and every tree, in the which is the fruit of a tree yielding seed; to you it shall be for meat.

Gen.9.3.bsb: Everything that lives and moves will be food for you; just as I gave you the green plants, I now give you all things.
Gen.9.3.kjv: Every moving thing that liveth shall be meat for you; even as the green herb have I given you all things.

Gen.21.2.bsb: So Sarah conceived and bore a son to Abraham in his old age, at the very time God had promised.
Gen.21.2.kjv: For Sarah conceived, and bare Abraham a son in his old age, at the set time of which God had spoken to him.

Gen.21.3.bsb: And Abraham gave the name Isaac to the son Sarah bore to him.
Gen.21.3.kjv: And Abraham called the name of his son that was born unto him, whom Sarah bare to him, Isaac.

Gen.21.4.bsb: When his son Isaac was eight days old, Abraham circumcised him, as God had commanded him.
Gen.21.4.kjv: And Abraham circumcised his son Isaac being eight days old, as God had commanded him.

Gen.21.5.bsb: Abraham was a hundred years old when his son Isaac was born to him.
Gen.21.5.kjv: And Abraham was an hundred years old, when his son Isaac was born unto him.

Gen.21.6.bsb: Then Sarah said, “God has made me laugh, and everyone who hears of this will laugh with me.”
Gen.21.6.kjv: And Sarah said, God hath made me to laugh, so that all that hear will laugh with me.

Gen.21.7.bsb: She added, “Who would have told Abraham that Sarah would nurse children? Yet I have borne him a son in his old age.”
Gen.21.7.kjv: And she said, Who would have said unto Abraham, that Sarah should have given children suck? for I have born him a son in his old age.

Gen.21.8.bsb: So the child grew and was weaned, and Abraham held a great feast on the day Isaac was weaned.
Gen.21.8.kjv: And the child grew, and was weaned: and Abraham made a great feast the same day that Isaac was weaned.

Gen.21.9.bsb: But Sarah saw that the son whom Hagar the Egyptian had borne to Abraham was mocking her son,
Gen.21.9.kjv: And Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian, which she had born unto Abraham, mocking.

Gen.21.10.bsb: and she said to Abraham, “Expel the slave woman and her son, for the slave woman’s son will never share in the inheritance with my son Isaac!”
Gen.21.10.kjv: Wherefore she said unto Abraham, Cast out this bondwoman and her son: for the son of this bondwoman shall not be heir with my son, even with Isaac.

Gen.21.11.bsb: Now this matter distressed Abraham greatly because it concerned his son Ishmael.
Gen.21.11.kjv: And the thing was very grievous in Abraham’s sight because of his son.

Gen.21.12.bsb: But God said to Abraham, “Do not be distressed about the boy and your maidservant. Listen to everything that Sarah tells you, for through Isaac your offspring will be reckoned.
Gen.21.12.kjv: And God said unto Abraham, Let it not be grievous in thy sight because of the lad, and because of thy bondwoman; in all that Sarah hath said unto thee, hearken unto her voice; for in Isaac shall thy seed be called.

Gen.21.13.bsb: But I will also make a nation of the slave woman’s son, because he is your offspring.”
Gen.21.13.kjv: And also of the son of the bondwoman will I make a nation, because he is thy seed.

Gen.21.14.bsb: Early in the morning, Abraham got up, took bread and a skin of water, put them on Hagar’s shoulders, and sent her away with the boy. She left and wandered in the Wilderness of Beersheba.
Gen.21.14.kjv: And Abraham rose up early in the morning, and took bread, and a bottle of water, and gave it unto Hagar, putting it on her shoulder, and the child, and sent her away: and she departed, and wandered in the wilderness of Beer–sheba.

Gen.21.15.bsb: When the water in the skin was gone, she left the boy under one of the bushes.
Gen.21.15.kjv: And the water was spent in the bottle, and she cast the child under one of the shrubs.

Gen.21.16.bsb: Then she went off and sat down nearby, about a bowshot away, for she said, “I cannot bear to watch the boy die!” And as she sat nearby, she lifted up her voice and wept.
Gen.21.16.kjv: And she went, and sat her down over against him a good way off, as it were a bowshot: for she said, Let me not see the death of the child. And she sat over against him, and lift up her voice, and wept.

Gen.21.17.bsb: Then God heard the voice of the boy, and the angel of God called to Hagar from heaven, “What is wrong, Hagar? Do not be afraid, for God has heard the voice of the boy where he lies.
Gen.21.17.kjv: And God heard the voice of the lad; and the angel of God called to Hagar out of heaven, and said unto her, What aileth thee, Hagar? fear not; for God hath heard the voice of the lad where he is.

Gen.21.18.bsb: Get up, lift up the boy, and take him by the hand, for I will make him into a great nation.”
Gen.21.18.kjv: Arise, lift up the lad, and hold him in thine hand; for I will make him a great nation.

Gen.21.19.bsb: Then God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water. So she went and filled the skin with water and gave the boy a drink.
Gen.21.19.kjv: And God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water; and she went, and filled the bottle with water, and gave the lad drink.

Gen.21.20.bsb: And God was with the boy, and he grew up and settled in the wilderness and became a great archer.
Gen.21.20.kjv: And God was with the lad; and he grew, and dwelt in the wilderness, and became an archer.

Gen.21.21.bsb: And while he was dwelling in the Wilderness of Paran, his mother got a wife for him from the land of Egypt.
Gen.21.21.kjv: And he dwelt in the wilderness of Paran: and his mother took him a wife out of the land of Egypt.

Gen.21.23.bsb: Now, therefore, swear to me here before God that you will not deal falsely with me or my children or descendants. Show to me and to the country in which you reside the same kindness that I have shown to you.”
Gen.21.23.kjv: Now therefore swear unto me here by God that thou wilt not deal falsely with me, nor with my son, nor with my son’s son: but according to the kindness that I have done unto thee, thou shalt do unto me, and to the land wherein thou hast sojourned.

Gen.7.22.bsb: Of all that was on dry land, everything that had the breath of life in its nostrils died.
Gen.7.22.kjv: All in whose nostrils was the breath of life, of all that was in the dry land, died.

Gen.2.19.bsb: And out of the ground the LORD God formed every beast of the field and every bird of the air, and He brought them to the man to see what he would name each one. And whatever the man called each living creature, that was its name.

Gen.3.9.bsb: But the LORD God called out to the man, “Where are you?”

Gen.3.21.kjv: Unto Adam also and to his wife did the Lord God make coats of skins, and clothed them.

Gen.3.18.bsb: Both thorns and thistles it will yield for you, and you will eat the plants of the field.

Gen.24.18.bsb: “Drink, my lord,” she replied, and she quickly lowered her jar to her hands and gave him a drink.
Gen.24.18.kjv: And she said, Drink, my lord: and she hasted, and let down her pitcher upon her hand, and gave him drink.

Gen.24.21.kjv: And the man wondering at her held his peace, to wit whether the Lord had made his journey prosperous or not.

Gen.24.23.bsb: “Whose daughter are you?” he asked. “Please tell me, is there room in your father’s house for us to spend the night?”
Gen.24.23.kjv: And said, Whose daughter art thou? tell me, I pray thee: is there room in thy father’s house for us to lodge in?

Gen.24.24.bsb: She replied, “I am the daughter of Bethuel, the son that Milcah bore to Nahor.”
Gen.24.24.kjv: And she said unto him, I am the daughter of Bethuel the son of Milcah, which she bare unto Nahor.

Gen.24.25.bsb: Then she added, “We have plenty of straw and feed, as well as a place for you to spend the night.”
Gen.24.25.kjv: She said moreover unto him, We have both straw and provender enough, and room to lodge in.

Gen.24.27.bsb: saying, “Blessed be the LORD, the God of my master Abraham, who has not withheld His kindness and faithfulness from my master. As for me, the LORD has led me on the journey to the house of my master’s relatives.”
Gen.24.27.kjv: And he said, Blessed be the Lord God of my master Abraham, who hath not left destitute my master of his mercy and his truth: I being in the way, the Lord led me to the house of my master’s brethren.

Gen.32.24.bsb: So Jacob was left all alone, and there a man wrestled with him until daybreak.
Gen.32.24.kjv: And Jacob was left alone; and there wrestled a man with him until the breaking of the day.

Gen.32.25.bsb: When the man saw that he could not overpower Jacob, he struck the socket of Jacob’s hip and dislocated it as they wrestled.
Gen.32.25.kjv: And when he saw that he prevailed not against him, he touched the hollow of his thigh; and the hollow of Jacob’s thigh was out of joint, as he wrestled with him.

Gen.32.27.bsb: “What is your name?” the man asked. “Jacob,” he replied.
Gen.32.27.kjv: And he said unto him, What is thy name? And he said, Jacob.

Gen.32.28.bsb: Then the man said, “Your name will no longer be Jacob, but Israel, because you have struggled with God and with men, and you have prevailed.”
Gen.32.28.kjv: And he said, Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel: for as a prince hast thou power with God and with men, and hast prevailed.

Gen.32.29.bsb: And Jacob requested, “Please tell me your name.” But he replied, “Why do you ask my name?” Then he blessed Jacob there.
Gen.32.29.kjv: And Jacob asked him, and said, Tell me, I pray thee, thy name. And he said, Wherefore is it that thou dost ask after my name? And he blessed him there.

Gen.32.30.bsb: So Jacob named the place Peniel, saying, “Indeed, I have seen God face to face, and yet my life was spared.”
Gen.32.30.kjv: And Jacob called the name of the place Peniel: for I have seen God face to face, and my life is preserved.

Gen.24.12.bsb: “O LORD, God of my master Abraham,” he prayed, “please grant me success today, and show kindness to my master Abraham.
Gen.24.12.kjv: And he said, O Lord God of my master Abraham, I pray thee, send me good speed this day, and shew kindness unto my master Abraham.

Gen.24.13.bsb: Here I am, standing beside the spring, and the daughters of the townspeople are coming out to draw water.
Gen.24.13.kjv: Behold, I stand here by the well of water; and the daughters of the men of the city come out to draw water:

Gen.24.14.bsb: Now may it happen that the girl to whom I say, ‘Please let down your jar that I may drink,’ and who responds, ‘Drink, and I will water your camels as well’—let her be the one You have appointed for Your servant Isaac. By this I will know that You have shown kindness to my master.”
Gen.24.14.kjv: And let it come to pass, that the damsel to whom I shall say, Let down thy pitcher, I pray thee, that I may drink; and she shall say, Drink, and I will give thy camels drink also: let the same be she that thou hast appointed for thy servant Isaac; and thereby shall I know that thou hast shewed kindness unto my master.

Gen.17.18.bsb: And Abraham said to God, “O that Ishmael might live under Your blessing!”
Gen.17.18.kjv: And Abraham said unto God, O that Ishmael might live before thee!

Gen.18.23.bsb: Abraham stepped forward and said, “Will You really sweep away the righteous with the wicked?
Gen.18.23.kjv: And Abraham drew near, and said, Wilt thou also destroy the righteous with the wicked?

Gen.18.24.bsb: What if there are fifty righteous ones in the city? Will You really sweep it away and not spare the place for the sake of the fifty righteous ones who are there?
Gen.18.24.kjv: Peradventure there be fifty righteous within the city: wilt thou also destroy and not spare the place for the fifty righteous that are therein?

Gen.18.25.bsb: Far be it from You to do such a thing—to kill the righteous with the wicked, so that the righteous and the wicked are treated alike. Far be it from You! Will not the Judge of all the earth do what is right?”
Gen.18.25.kjv: That be far from thee to do after this manner, to slay the righteous with the wicked: and that the righteous should be as the wicked, that be far from thee: Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right?

Gen.18.26.bsb: So the LORD replied, “If I find fifty righteous ones within the city of Sodom, on their account I will spare the whole place.”
Gen.18.26.kjv: And the Lord said, If I find in Sodom fifty righteous within the city, then I will spare all the place for their sakes.

Gen.18.28.bsb: suppose the fifty righteous ones lack five. Will You destroy the whole city for the lack of five?” He replied, “If I find forty-five there, I will not destroy it.”
Gen.18.28.kjv: Peradventure there shall lack five of the fifty righteous: wilt thou destroy all the city for lack of five? And he said, If I find there forty and five, I will not destroy it.

Gen.18.29.bsb: Once again Abraham spoke to the LORD, “Suppose forty are found there?” He answered, “On account of the forty, I will not do it.”
Gen.18.29.kjv: And he spake unto him yet again, and said, Peradventure there shall be forty found there. And he said, I will not do it for forty’s sake.

Gen.18.30.bsb: Then Abraham said, “May the Lord not be angry, but let me speak further. Suppose thirty are found there?” He replied, “If I find thirty there, I will not do it.”
Gen.18.30.kjv: And he said unto him, Oh let not the Lord be angry, and I will speak: Peradventure there shall thirty be found there. And he said, I will not do it, if I find thirty there.

Gen.18.31.bsb: And Abraham said, “Now that I have ventured to speak to the Lord, suppose twenty are found there?” He answered, “On account of the twenty, I will not destroy it.”
Gen.18.31.kjv: And he said, Behold now, I have taken upon me to speak unto the Lord: Peradventure there shall be twenty found there. And he said, I will not destroy it for twenty’s sake.

Gen.18.32.bsb: Finally, Abraham said, “May the Lord not be angry, but let me speak once more. Suppose ten are found there?” And He answered, “On account of the ten, I will not destroy it.”
Gen.18.32.kjv: And he said, Oh let not the Lord be angry, and I will speak yet but this once: Peradventure ten shall be found there. And he said, I will not destroy it for ten’s sake.

Gen.2.1.kjv: Thus the heavens and the earth were finished, and all the host of them.

Gen.32.2.bsb: When Jacob saw them, he said, “This is the camp of God.” So he named that place Mahanaim.
Gen.32.2.kjv: And when Jacob saw them, he said, This is God’s host: and he called the name of that place Mahanaim.

Gen.24.7.bsb: The LORD, the God of heaven, who brought me from my father’s house and my native land, who spoke to me and promised me on oath, saying, ‘To your offspring I will give this land’—He will send His angel before you so that you can take a wife for my son from there.
Gen.24.7.kjv: The Lord God of heaven, which took me from my father’s house, and from the land of my kindred, and which spake unto me, and that sware unto me, saying, Unto thy seed will I give this land; he shall send his angel before thee, and thou shalt take a wife unto my son from thence.

Gen.24.40.bsb: And he told me, ‘The LORD, before whom I have walked, will send His angel with you and make your journey a success, so that you may take a wife for my son from my kindred and from my father’s house.
Gen.24.40.kjv: And he said unto me, The Lord, before whom I walk, will send his angel with thee, and prosper thy way; and thou shalt take a wife for my son of my kindred, and of my father’s house:

Gen.19.1.bsb: Now the two angels arrived at Sodom in the evening, and Lot was sitting in the gateway of the city. When Lot saw them, he got up to meet them, bowed facedown,
Gen.19.1.kjv: And there came two angels to Sodom at even; and Lot sat in the gate of Sodom: and Lot seeing them rose up to meet them; and he bowed himself with his face toward the ground;

Gen.19.2.bsb: and said, “My lords, please turn aside into the house of your servant; wash your feet and spend the night. Then you can rise early and go on your way.” “No,” they answered, “we will spend the night in the square.”
Gen.19.2.kjv: And he said, Behold now, my lords, turn in, I pray you, into your servant’s house, and tarry all night, and wash your feet, and ye shall rise up early, and go on your ways. And they said, Nay; but we will abide in the street all night.

Gen.19.3.bsb: But Lot insisted so strongly that they followed him into his house. He prepared a feast for them and baked unleavened bread, and they ate.
Gen.19.3.kjv: And he pressed upon them greatly; and they turned in unto him, and entered into his house; and he made them a feast, and did bake unleavened bread, and they did eat.

Gen.19.4.bsb: Before they had gone to bed, all the men of the city of Sodom, both young and old, surrounded the house.
Gen.19.4.kjv: But before they lay down, the men of the city, even the men of Sodom, compassed the house round, both old and young, all the people from every quarter:

Gen.19.5.bsb: They called out to Lot, saying, “Where are the men who came to you tonight? Send them out to us so we can have relations with them!”
Gen.19.5.kjv: And they called unto Lot, and said unto him, Where are the men which came in to thee this night? bring them out unto us, that we may know them.

Gen.19.6.bsb: Lot went outside to meet them, shutting the door behind him.
Gen.19.6.kjv: And Lot went out at the door unto them, and shut the door after him,

Gen.19.7.bsb: “Please, my brothers,” he pleaded, “don’t do such a wicked thing!
Gen.19.7.kjv: And said, I pray you, brethren, do not so wickedly.

Gen.19.8.bsb: Look, I have two daughters who have never slept with a man. Let me bring them to you, and you can do to them as you please. But do not do anything to these men, for they have come under the protection of my roof.”
Gen.19.8.kjv: Behold now, I have two daughters which have not known man; let me, I pray you, bring them out unto you, and do ye to them as is good in your eyes: only unto these men do nothing; for therefore came they under the shadow of my roof.

Gen.19.9.bsb: “Get out of the way!” they replied. And they declared, “This one came here as a foreigner, and he is already acting like a judge! Now we will treat you worse than them.” And they pressed in on Lot and moved in to break down the door.
Gen.19.9.kjv: And they said, Stand back. And they said again, This one fellow came in to sojourn, and he will needs be a judge: now will we deal worse with thee, than with them. And they pressed sore upon the man, even Lot, and came near to break the door.

Gen.19.10.bsb: But the men inside reached out, pulled Lot into the house with them, and shut the door.
Gen.19.10.kjv: But the men put forth their hand, and pulled Lot into the house to them, and shut to the door.

Gen.19.11.bsb: And they struck the men at the entrance, young and old, with blindness, so that they wearied themselves trying to find the door.
Gen.19.11.kjv: And they smote the men that were at the door of the house with blindness, both small and great: so that they wearied themselves to find the door.

Gen.19.12.bsb: Then the two men said to Lot, “Do you have anyone else here—a son-in-law, your sons or daughters, or anyone else in the city who belongs to you? Get them out of here,
Gen.19.12.kjv: And the men said unto Lot, Hast thou here any besides? son in law, and thy sons, and thy daughters, and whatsoever thou hast in the city, bring them out of this place:

Gen.19.13.bsb: because we are about to destroy this place. For the outcry to the LORD against its people is so great that He has sent us to destroy it.”
Gen.19.13.kjv: For we will destroy this place, because the cry of them is waxen great before the face of the Lord; and the Lord hath sent us to destroy it.

Gen.19.14.bsb: So Lot went out and spoke to the sons-in-law who were pledged in marriage to his daughters. “Get up,” he said. “Get out of this place, for the LORD is about to destroy the city!” But his sons-in-law thought he was joking.
Gen.19.14.kjv: And Lot went out, and spake unto his sons in law, which married his daughters, and said, Up, get you out of this place; for the Lord will destroy this city. But he seemed as one that mocked unto his sons in law.

Gen.19.15.bsb: At daybreak the angels hurried Lot along, saying, “Get up! Take your wife and your two daughters who are here, or you will be swept away in the punishment of the city.”
Gen.19.15.kjv: And when the morning arose, then the angels hastened Lot, saying, Arise, take thy wife, and thy two daughters, which are here; lest thou be consumed in the iniquity of the city.

Gen.19.16.bsb: But when Lot hesitated, the men grabbed his hand and the hands of his wife and his two daughters. And they led them safely out of the city, because of the LORD’s compassion for them.
Gen.19.16.kjv: And while he lingered, the men laid hold upon his hand, and upon the hand of his wife, and upon the hand of his two daughters; the Lord being merciful unto him: and they brought him forth, and set him without the city.

Gen.19.17.bsb: As soon as the men had brought them out, one of them said, “Run for your lives! Do not look back, and do not stop anywhere on the plain! Flee to the mountains, or you will be swept away!”
Gen.19.17.kjv: And it came to pass, when they had brought them forth abroad, that he said, Escape for thy life; look not behind thee, neither stay thou in all the plain; escape to the mountain, lest thou be consumed.

Gen.19.18.bsb: But Lot replied, “No, my lords, please!
Gen.19.18.kjv: And Lot said unto them, Oh, not so, my Lord:

Gen.19.22.bsb: Hurry! Run there quickly, for I cannot do anything until you reach it.” That is why the town was called Zoar.
Gen.19.22.kjv: Haste thee, escape thither; for I cannot do any thing till thou be come thither. Therefore the name of the city was called Zoar.

Gen.19.23.bsb: And by the time the sun had risen over the land, Lot had reached Zoar.
Gen.19.23.kjv: The sun was risen upon the earth when Lot entered into Zoar.

Gen.19.24.bsb: Then the LORD rained down sulfur and fire on Sodom and Gomorrah—from the LORD out of the heavens.
Gen.19.24.kjv: Then the Lord rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from the Lord out of heaven;

Gen.19.25.bsb: Thus He destroyed these cities and the entire plain, including all the inhabitants of the cities and everything that grew on the ground.
Gen.19.25.kjv: And he overthrew those cities, and all the plain, and all the inhabitants of the cities, and that which grew upon the ground.

Gen.18.2.bsb: And Abraham looked up and saw three men standing nearby. When he saw them, he ran from the entrance of his tent to meet them and bowed low to the ground.
Gen.18.2.kjv: And he lift up his eyes and looked, and, lo, three men stood by him: and when he saw them, he ran to meet them from the tent door, and bowed himself toward the ground,

Gen.22.12.bsb: “Do not lay a hand on the boy or do anything to him,” said the angel, “for now I know that you fear God, since you have not withheld your only son from me.”
Gen.22.12.kjv: And he said, Lay not thine hand upon the lad, neither do thou any thing unto him: for now I know that thou fearest God, seeing thou hast not withheld thy son, thine only son from me.

Gen.22.13.bsb: Then Abraham looked up and saw behind him a ram in a thicket, caught by its horns. So he went and took the ram and offered it as a burnt offering in place of his son.
Gen.22.13.kjv: And Abraham lifted up his eyes, and looked, and behold behind him a ram caught in a thicket by his horns: and Abraham went and took the ram, and offered him up for a burnt offering in the stead of his son.

Gen.22.14.bsb: And Abraham called that place The LORD Will Provide. So to this day it is said, “On the mountain of the LORD it will be provided.”
Gen.22.14.kjv: And Abraham called the name of that place Jehovah–jireh: as it is said to this day, In the mount of the Lord it shall be seen.

Gen.22.15.bsb: And the angel of the LORD called to Abraham from heaven a second time,
Gen.22.15.kjv: And the angel of the Lord called unto Abraham out of heaven the second time,

Gen.22.16.bsb: saying, “By Myself I have sworn, declares the LORD, that because you have done this and have not withheld your only son,
Gen.22.16.kjv: And said, By myself have I sworn, saith the Lord, for because thou hast done this thing, and hast not withheld thy son, thine only son:

Gen.22.17.bsb: I will surely bless you, and I will multiply your descendants like the stars in the sky and the sand on the seashore. Your descendants will possess the gates of their enemies.
Gen.22.17.kjv: That in blessing I will bless thee, and in multiplying I will multiply thy seed as the stars of the heaven, and as the sand which is upon the sea shore; and thy seed shall possess the gate of his enemies;

Gen.28.12.bsb: And Jacob had a dream about a ladder that rested on the earth with its top reaching up to heaven, and God’s angels were going up and down the ladder.
Gen.28.12.kjv: And he dreamed, and behold a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven: and behold the angels of God ascending and descending on it.

Gen.4.6.bsb: “Why are you angry,” said the LORD to Cain, “and why has your countenance fallen?
Gen.4.6.kjv: And the Lord said unto Cain, Why art thou wroth? and why is thy countenance fallen?

Gen.49.7.bsb: Cursed be their anger, for it is strong, and their wrath, for it is cruel! I will disperse them in Jacob and scatter them in Israel.
Gen.49.7.kjv: Cursed be their anger, for it was fierce; and their wrath, for it was cruel: I will divide them in Jacob, and scatter them in Israel.

Gen.4.5.bsb: but He had no regard for Cain and his offering. So Cain became very angry, and his countenance fell.
Gen.4.5.kjv: But unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect. And Cain was very wroth, and his countenance fell.

Gen.4.7.bsb: If you do what is right, will you not be accepted? But if you refuse to do what is right, sin is crouching at your door; it desires you, but you must master it.”
Gen.4.7.kjv: If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door. And unto thee shall be his desire, and thou shalt rule over him.

Gen.4.8.bsb: Then Cain said to his brother Abel, “Let us go out to the field.” And while they were in the field, Cain rose up against his brother Abel and killed him.
Gen.4.8.kjv: And Cain talked with Abel his brother: and it came to pass, when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.

Gen.49.5.bsb: Simeon and Levi are brothers; their swords are weapons of violence.
Gen.49.5.kjv: Simeon and Levi are brethren; instruments of cruelty are in their habitations.

Gen.49.6.bsb: May I never enter their council; may I never join their assembly. For they kill men in their anger, and hamstring oxen on a whim.
Gen.49.6.kjv: O my soul, come not thou into their secret; unto their assembly, mine honour, be not thou united: for in their anger they slew a man, and in their selfwill they digged down a wall.

Gen.6.6.bsb: And the LORD regretted that He had made man on the earth, and He was grieved in His heart.
Gen.6.6.kjv: And it repented the Lord that he had made man on the earth, and it grieved him at his heart.

Gen.9.16.bsb: And whenever the rainbow appears in the clouds, I will see it and remember the everlasting covenant between God and every living creature of every kind that is on the earth.”
Gen.9.16.kjv: And the bow shall be in the cloud; and I will look upon it, that I may remember the everlasting covenant between God and every living creature of all flesh that is upon the earth.

Gen.11.5.bsb: Then the LORD came down to see the city and the tower that the sons of men were building.
Gen.11.5.kjv: And the Lord came down to see the city and the tower, which the children of men builded.

Gen.11.7.bsb: Come, let Us go down and confuse their language, so that they will not understand one another’s speech.”
Gen.11.7.kjv: Go to, let us go down, and there confound their language, that they may not understand one another’s speech.

Gen.18.17.bsb: And the LORD said, “Shall I hide from Abraham what I am about to do?
Gen.18.17.kjv: And the Lord said, Shall I hide from Abraham that thing which I do;

Gen.18.18.bsb: Abraham will surely become a great and powerful nation, and through him all the nations of the earth will be blessed.
Gen.18.18.kjv: Seeing that Abraham shall surely become a great and mighty nation, and all the nations of the earth shall be blessed in him?

Gen.18.19.bsb: For I have chosen him, so that he will command his children and his household after him to keep the way of the LORD by doing what is right and just, in order that the LORD may bring upon Abraham what He has promised.”
Gen.18.19.kjv: For I know him, that he will command his children and his household after him, and they shall keep the way of the Lord, to do justice and judgment; that the Lord may bring upon Abraham that which he hath spoken of him.

Gen.18.21.bsb: I will go down to see if their actions fully justify the outcry that has reached Me. If not, I will find out.”
Gen.18.21.kjv: I will go down now, and see whether they have done altogether according to the cry of it, which is come unto me; and if not, I will know.

Gen.18.33.bsb: When the LORD had finished speaking with Abraham, He departed, and Abraham returned home.
Gen.18.33.kjv: And the Lord went his way, as soon as he had left communing with Abraham: and Abraham returned unto his place.

Gen.19.29.bsb: So when God destroyed the cities of the plain, He remembered Abraham, and He brought Lot out of the catastrophe that destroyed the cities where he had lived.
Gen.19.29.kjv: And it came to pass, when God destroyed the cities of the plain, that God remembered Abraham, and sent Lot out of the midst of the overthrow, when he overthrew the cities in the which Lot dwelt.

Gen.28.13.bsb: And there at the top the LORD was standing and saying, “I am the LORD, the God of your father Abraham and the God of Isaac. I will give you and your descendants the land on which you now lie.
Gen.28.13.kjv: And, behold, the Lord stood above it, and said, I am the Lord God of Abraham thy father, and the God of Isaac: the land whereon thou liest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed;

Gen.35.13.bsb: Then God went up from the place where He had spoken with him.
Gen.35.13.kjv: And God went up from him in the place where he talked with him.

Gen.41.14.bsb: So Pharaoh sent for Joseph, who was quickly brought out of the dungeon. After he had shaved and changed his clothes, he went in before Pharaoh.
Gen.41.14.kjv: Then Pharaoh sent and called Joseph, and they brought him hastily out of the dungeon: and he shaved himself, and changed his raiment, and came in unto Pharaoh.

Gen.9.1.bsb: And God blessed Noah and his sons and said to them, “Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth.
Gen.9.1.kjv: And God blessed Noah and his sons, and said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth.

Gen.9.2.bsb: The fear and dread of you will fall on every living creature on the earth, every bird of the air, every creature that crawls on the ground, and all the fish of the sea. They are delivered into your hand.
Gen.9.2.kjv: And the fear of you and the dread of you shall be upon every beast of the earth, and upon every fowl of the air, upon all that moveth upon the earth, and upon all the fishes of the sea; into your hand are they delivered.

Gen.14.19.bsb: and he blessed Abram and said: “Blessed be Abram by God Most High, Creator of heaven and earth,
Gen.14.19.kjv: And he blessed him, and said, Blessed be Abram of the most high God, possessor of heaven and earth:

Gen.14.20.bsb: and blessed be God Most High, who has delivered your enemies into your hand.” Then Abram gave Melchizedek a tenth of everything.
Gen.14.20.kjv: And blessed be the most high God, which hath delivered thine enemies into thy hand. And he gave him tithes of all.

Gen.24.60.bsb: And they blessed Rebekah and said to her, “Our sister, may you become the mother of thousands upon thousands. May your offspring possess the gates of their enemies.”
Gen.24.60.kjv: And they blessed Rebekah, and said unto her, Thou art our sister, be thou the mother of thousands of millions, and let thy seed possess the gate of those which hate them.

Gen.27.23.bsb: Isaac did not recognize him, because his hands were hairy like those of his brother Esau; so he blessed him.
Gen.27.23.kjv: And he discerned him not, because his hands were hairy, as his brother Esau’s hands: so he blessed him.

Gen.27.24.bsb: Again he asked, “Are you really my son Esau?” And he replied, “I am.”
Gen.27.24.kjv: And he said, Art thou my very son Esau? And he said, I am.

Gen.27.25.bsb: “Serve me,” said Isaac, “and let me eat some of my son’s game, so that I may bless you.” Jacob brought it to him, and he ate; then he brought him wine, and he drank.
Gen.27.25.kjv: And he said, Bring it near to me, and I will eat of my son’s venison, that my soul may bless thee. And he brought it near to him, and he did eat: and he brought him wine, and he drank.

Gen.27.26.bsb: Then his father Isaac said to him, “Please come near and kiss me, my son.”
Gen.27.26.kjv: And his father Isaac said unto him, Come near now, and kiss me, my son.

Gen.27.27.bsb: So he came near and kissed him. When Isaac smelled his clothing, he blessed him and said: “Ah, the smell of my son is like the smell of a field that the LORD has blessed.
Gen.27.27.kjv: And he came near, and kissed him: and he smelled the smell of his raiment, and blessed him, and said, See, the smell of my son is as the smell of a field which the Lord hath blessed:

Gen.27.28.bsb: May God give to you the dew of heaven and the richness of the earth—an abundance of grain and new wine.
Gen.27.28.kjv: Therefore God give thee of the dew of heaven, and the fatness of the earth, and plenty of corn and wine:

Gen.27.29.bsb: May peoples serve you and nations bow down to you. May you be the master of your brothers, and may the sons of your mother bow down to you. May those who curse you be cursed, and those who bless you be blessed.”
Gen.27.29.kjv: Let people serve thee, and nations bow down to thee: be lord over thy brethren, and let thy mother’s sons bow down to thee: cursed be every one that curseth thee, and blessed be he that blesseth thee.

Gen.27.37.bsb: But Isaac answered Esau: “Look, I have made him your master and given him all his relatives as servants; I have sustained him with grain and new wine. What is left that I can do for you, my son?”
Gen.27.37.kjv: And Isaac answered and said unto Esau, Behold, I have made him thy lord, and all his brethren have I given to him for servants; and with corn and wine have I sustained him: and what shall I do now unto thee, my son?

Gen.28.1.bsb: So Isaac called for Jacob and blessed him. “Do not take a wife from the Canaanite women,” he commanded.
Gen.28.1.kjv: And Isaac called Jacob, and blessed him, and charged him, and said unto him, Thou shalt not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan.

Gen.28.2.bsb: “Go at once to Paddan-aram, to the house of your mother’s father Bethuel, and take a wife from among the daughters of Laban, your mother’s brother.
Gen.28.2.kjv: Arise, go to Padan–aram, to the house of Bethuel thy mother’s father; and take thee a wife from thence of the daughters of Laban thy mother’s brother.

Gen.28.3.bsb: May God Almighty bless you and make you fruitful and multiply you, so that you may become a company of peoples.
Gen.28.3.kjv: And God Almighty bless thee, and make thee fruitful, and multiply thee, that thou mayest be a multitude of people;

Gen.28.4.bsb: And may He give the blessing of Abraham to you and your descendants, so that you may possess the land where you dwell as a foreigner, the land God gave to Abraham.”
Gen.28.4.kjv: And give thee the blessing of Abraham, to thee, and to thy seed with thee; that thou mayest inherit the land wherein thou art a stranger, which God gave unto Abraham.

Gen.27.39.bsb: His father Isaac answered him: “Behold, your dwelling place shall be away from the richness of the land, away from the dew of heaven above.
Gen.27.39.kjv: And Isaac his father answered and said unto him, Behold, thy dwelling shall be the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of heaven from above;

Gen.27.40.bsb: You shall live by the sword and serve your brother. But when you rebel, you will tear his yoke from your neck.”
Gen.27.40.kjv: And by thy sword shalt thou live, and shalt serve thy brother; and it shall come to pass when thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck.

Gen.47.7.bsb: Then Joseph brought in his father Jacob and presented him before Pharaoh, and Jacob blessed Pharaoh.
Gen.47.7.kjv: And Joseph brought in Jacob his father, and set him before Pharaoh: and Jacob blessed Pharaoh.

Gen.47.8.bsb: “How many years have you lived?” Pharaoh asked.
Gen.47.8.kjv: And Pharaoh said unto Jacob, How old art thou?

Gen.47.9.bsb: “My travels have lasted 130 years,” Jacob replied. “My years have been few and hard, and they have not matched the years of the travels of my fathers.”
Gen.47.9.kjv: And Jacob said unto Pharaoh, The days of the years of my pilgrimage are an hundred and thirty years: few and evil have the days of the years of my life been, and have not attained unto the days of the years of the life of my fathers in the days of their pilgrimage.

Gen.47.10.bsb: Then Jacob blessed Pharaoh and departed from his presence.
Gen.47.10.kjv: And Jacob blessed Pharaoh, and went out from before Pharaoh.

Gen.27.1.bsb: When Isaac was old and his eyes were so weak that he could no longer see, he called his older son Esau and said to him, “My son.” “Here I am,” Esau replied.
Gen.27.1.kjv: And it came to pass, that when Isaac was old, and his eyes were dim, so that he could not see, he called Esau his eldest son, and said unto him, My son: and he said unto him, Behold, here am I.

Gen.48.10.bsb: Now Israel’s eyesight was poor because of old age; he could hardly see. Joseph brought his sons to him, and his father kissed them and embraced them.
Gen.48.10.kjv: Now the eyes of Israel were dim for age, so that he could not see. And he brought them near unto him; and he kissed them, and embraced them.

Gen.24.53.bsb: Then he brought out jewels of silver and gold, and articles of clothing, and he gave them to Rebekah. He also gave precious gifts to her brother and her mother.
Gen.24.53.kjv: And the servant brought forth jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and raiment, and gave them to Rebekah: he gave also to her brother and to her mother precious things.

Gen.24.59.bsb: So they sent their sister Rebekah on her way, along with her nurse and Abraham’s servant and his men.
Gen.24.59.kjv: And they sent away Rebekah their sister, and her nurse, and Abraham’s servant, and his men.

Gen.24.61.bsb: Then Rebekah and her servant girls got ready, mounted the camels, and followed the man. So the servant took Rebekah and left.
Gen.24.61.kjv: And Rebekah arose, and her damsels, and they rode upon the camels, and followed the man: and the servant took Rebekah, and went his way.

Gen.29.24.bsb: And Laban gave his servant girl Zilpah to his daughter Leah as her maidservant.
Gen.29.24.kjv: And Laban gave unto his daughter Leah Zilpah his maid for an handmaid.

Gen.29.29.bsb: Laban also gave his servant girl Bilhah to his daughter Rachel as her maidservant.
Gen.29.29.kjv: And Laban gave to Rachel his daughter Bilhah his handmaid to be her maid.

Gen.14.12.bsb: They also carried off Abram’s nephew Lot and his possessions, since Lot was living in Sodom.
Gen.14.12.kjv: And they took Lot, Abram’s brother’s son, who dwelt in Sodom, and his goods, and departed.

Gen.41.39.bsb: Then Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Since God has made all this known to you, there is no one as discerning and wise as you.
Gen.41.39.kjv: And Pharaoh said unto Joseph, Forasmuch as God hath shewed thee all this, there is none so discreet and wise as thou art:

Gen.41.40.bsb: You shall be in charge of my house, and all my people are to obey your commands. Only with regard to the throne will I be greater than you.”
Gen.41.40.kjv: Thou shalt be over my house, and according unto thy word shall all my people be ruled: only in the throne will I be greater than thou.

Gen.41.41.bsb: Pharaoh also told Joseph, “I hereby place you over all the land of Egypt.”
Gen.41.41.kjv: And Pharaoh said unto Joseph, See, I have set thee over all the land of Egypt.

Gen.41.42.bsb: Then Pharaoh removed the signet ring from his finger, put it on Joseph’s finger, clothed him in garments of fine linen, and placed a gold chain around his neck.
Gen.41.42.kjv: And Pharaoh took off his ring from his hand, and put it upon Joseph’s hand, and arrayed him in vestures of fine linen, and put a gold chain about his neck;

Gen.41.43.bsb: He had Joseph ride in his second chariot, with men calling out before him, “Bow the knee!” So he placed him over all the land of Egypt.
Gen.41.43.kjv: And he made him to ride in the second chariot which he had; and they cried before him, Bow the knee: and he made him ruler over all the land of Egypt.

Gen.41.44.bsb: And Pharaoh declared to Joseph, “I am Pharaoh, but without your permission, no one in all the land of Egypt shall lift his hand or foot.”
Gen.41.44.kjv: And Pharaoh said unto Joseph, I am Pharaoh, and without thee shall no man lift up his hand or foot in all the land of Egypt.

Gen.41.45.bsb: Pharaoh gave Joseph the name Zaphenath-paneah, and he gave him Asenath daughter of Potiphera, priest of On, to be his wife. And Joseph took charge of all the land of Egypt.
Gen.41.45.kjv: And Pharaoh called Joseph’s name Zaphnath–paaneah; and he gave him to wife Asenath the daughter of Poti–pherah priest of On. And Joseph went out over all the land of Egypt.

Gen.15.2.bsb: But Abram replied, “O Lord GOD, what can You give me, since I remain childless, and the heir of my house is Eliezer of Damascus?”
Gen.15.2.kjv: And Abram said, Lord God, what wilt thou give me, seeing I go childless, and the steward of my house is this Eliezer of Damascus?

Gen.15.4.bsb: Then the word of the LORD came to Abram, saying, “This one will not be your heir, but one who comes from your own body will be your heir.”
Gen.15.4.kjv: And, behold, the word of the Lord came unto him, saying, This shall not be thine heir; but he that shall come forth out of thine own bowels shall be thine heir.

Gen.15.5.bsb: And the LORD took him outside and said, “Now look to the heavens and count the stars, if you are able.” Then He told him, “So shall your offspring be.”
Gen.15.5.kjv: And he brought him forth abroad, and said, Look now toward heaven, and tell the stars, if thou be able to number them: and he said unto him, So shall thy seed be.

Gen.21.1.bsb: Now the LORD attended to Sarah as He had said, and the LORD did for Sarah what He had promised.
Gen.21.1.kjv: And the Lord visited Sarah as he had said, and the Lord did unto Sarah as he had spoken.

Gen.25.21.bsb: Later, Isaac prayed to the LORD on behalf of his wife, because she was barren. And the LORD heard his prayer, and his wife Rebekah conceived.
Gen.25.21.kjv: And Isaac intreated the Lord for his wife, because she was barren: and the Lord was intreated of him, and Rebekah his wife conceived.

Gen.30.17.bsb: And God listened to Leah, and she conceived and bore a fifth son to Jacob.
Gen.30.17.kjv: And God hearkened unto Leah, and she conceived, and bare Jacob the fifth son.

Gen.30.18.bsb: Then Leah said, “God has rewarded me for giving my maidservant to my husband.” So she named him Issachar.
Gen.30.18.kjv: And Leah said, God hath given me my hire, because I have given my maiden to my husband: and she called his name Issachar.

Gen.30.19.bsb: Again Leah conceived and bore a sixth son to Jacob.
Gen.30.19.kjv: And Leah conceived again, and bare Jacob the sixth son.

Gen.30.20.bsb: “God has given me a good gift,” she said. “This time my husband will honor me, because I have borne him six sons.” And she named him Zebulun.
Gen.30.20.kjv: And Leah said, God hath endued me with a good dowry; now will my husband dwell with me, because I have born him six sons: and she called his name Zebulun.

Gen.30.21.bsb: After that, Leah gave birth to a daughter and named her Dinah.
Gen.30.21.kjv: And afterwards she bare a daughter, and called her name Dinah.

Gen.30.22.bsb: Then God remembered Rachel. He listened to her and opened her womb,
Gen.30.22.kjv: And God remembered Rachel, and God hearkened to her, and opened her womb.

Gen.30.23.bsb: and she conceived and gave birth to a son. “God has taken away my shame,” she said.
Gen.30.23.kjv: And she conceived, and bare a son; and said, God hath taken away my reproach:

Gen.30.24.bsb: She named him Joseph, and said, “May the LORD add to me another son.”
Gen.30.24.kjv: And she called his name Joseph; and said, The Lord shall add to me another son.

Gen.27.6.bsb: Rebekah said to her son Jacob, “Behold, I overheard your father saying to your brother Esau,
Gen.27.6.kjv: And Rebekah spake unto Jacob her son, saying, Behold, I heard thy father speak unto Esau thy brother, saying,

Gen.27.7.bsb: ‘Bring me some game and prepare me a tasty dish to eat, so that I may bless you in the presence of the LORD before I die.’
Gen.27.7.kjv: Bring me venison, and make me savoury meat, that I may eat, and bless thee before the Lord before my death.

Gen.27.8.bsb: Now, my son, listen to my voice and do exactly as I tell you.
Gen.27.8.kjv: Now therefore, my son, obey my voice according to that which I command thee.

Gen.27.9.bsb: Go out to the flock and bring me two choice young goats, so that I can make them into a tasty dish for your father—the kind he loves.
Gen.27.9.kjv: Go now to the flock, and fetch me from thence two good kids of the goats; and I will make them savoury meat for thy father, such as he loveth:

Gen.27.10.bsb: Then take it to your father to eat, so that he may bless you before he dies.”
Gen.27.10.kjv: And thou shalt bring it to thy father, that he may eat, and that he may bless thee before his death.

Gen.27.11.bsb: Jacob answered his mother Rebekah, “Look, my brother Esau is a hairy man, but I am smooth-skinned.
Gen.27.11.kjv: And Jacob said to Rebekah his mother, Behold, Esau my brother is a hairy man, and I am a smooth man:

Gen.27.12.bsb: What if my father touches me? Then I would be revealed to him as a deceiver, and I would bring upon myself a curse rather than a blessing.”
Gen.27.12.kjv: My father peradventure will feel me, and I shall seem to him as a deceiver; and I shall bring a curse upon me, and not a blessing.

Gen.27.13.bsb: His mother replied, “Your curse be on me, my son. Just obey my voice and go get them for me.”
Gen.27.13.kjv: And his mother said unto him, Upon me be thy curse, my son: only obey my voice, and go fetch me them.

Gen.27.14.bsb: So Jacob went and got two goats and brought them to his mother, who made the tasty food his father loved.
Gen.27.14.kjv: And he went, and fetched, and brought them to his mother: and his mother made savoury meat, such as his father loved.

Gen.27.15.bsb: And Rebekah took the finest clothes in the house that belonged to her older son Esau, and she put them on her younger son Jacob.
Gen.27.15.kjv: And Rebekah took goodly raiment of her eldest son Esau, which were with her in the house, and put them upon Jacob her younger son:

Gen.27.16.bsb: She also put the skins of the young goats on his hands and on the smooth part of his neck.
Gen.27.16.kjv: And she put the skins of the kids of the goats upon his hands, and upon the smooth of his neck:

Gen.27.17.bsb: Then she handed her son Jacob the tasty food and bread she had made.
Gen.27.17.kjv: And she gave the savoury meat and the bread, which she had prepared, into the hand of her son Jacob.

Gen.37.3.bsb: Now Israel loved Joseph more than his other sons, because Joseph had been born to him in his old age; so he made him a robe of many colors.
Gen.37.3.kjv: Now Israel loved Joseph more than all his children, because he was the son of his old age: and he made him a coat of many colours.

Gen.37.4.bsb: When Joseph’s brothers saw that their father loved him more than any of them, they hated him and could not speak a kind word to him.
Gen.37.4.kjv: And when his brethren saw that their father loved him more than all his brethren, they hated him, and could not speak peaceably unto him.

Gen.29.15.bsb: Laban said to him, “Just because you are my relative, should you work for nothing? Tell me what your wages should be.”
Gen.29.15.kjv: And Laban said unto Jacob, Because thou art my brother, shouldest thou therefore serve me for nought? tell me, what shall thy wages be?

Gen.29.16.bsb: Now Laban had two daughters; the older was named Leah, and the younger was named Rachel.
Gen.29.16.kjv: And Laban had two daughters: the name of the elder was Leah, and the name of the younger was Rachel.

Gen.29.17.bsb: Leah had weak eyes, but Rachel was shapely and beautiful.
Gen.29.17.kjv: Leah was tender eyed; but Rachel was beautiful and well favoured.

Gen.29.18.bsb: Since Jacob loved Rachel, he answered, “I will serve you seven years for your younger daughter Rachel.”
Gen.29.18.kjv: And Jacob loved Rachel; and said, I will serve thee seven years for Rachel thy younger daughter.

Gen.29.19.bsb: Laban replied, “Better that I give her to you than to another. Stay here with me.”
Gen.29.19.kjv: And Laban said, It is better that I give her to thee, than that I should give her to another man: abide with me.

Gen.29.20.bsb: So Jacob served seven years for Rachel, yet it seemed but a few days because of his love for her.
Gen.29.20.kjv: And Jacob served seven years for Rachel; and they seemed unto him but a few days, for the love he had to her.

Gen.29.21.bsb: Finally Jacob said to Laban, “Grant me my wife, for my time is complete, and I want to sleep with her.”
Gen.29.21.kjv: And Jacob said unto Laban, Give me my wife, for my days are fulfilled, that I may go in unto her.

Gen.29.22.bsb: So Laban invited all the men of that place and prepared a feast.
Gen.29.22.kjv: And Laban gathered together all the men of the place, and made a feast.

Gen.29.23.bsb: But when evening came, Laban took his daughter Leah and gave her to Jacob, and he slept with her.
Gen.29.23.kjv: And it came to pass in the evening, that he took Leah his daughter, and brought her to him; and he went in unto her.

Gen.29.25.bsb: When morning came, there was Leah! “What have you done to me?” Jacob said to Laban. “Wasn’t it for Rachel that I served you? Why have you deceived me?”
Gen.29.25.kjv: And it came to pass, that in the morning, behold, it was Leah: and he said to Laban, What is this thou hast done unto me? did not I serve with thee for Rachel? wherefore then hast thou beguiled me?

Gen.29.26.bsb: Laban replied, “It is not our custom here to give the younger daughter in marriage before the older.
Gen.29.26.kjv: And Laban said, It must not be so done in our country, to give the younger before the firstborn.

Gen.29.27.bsb: Finish this week’s celebration, and we will give you the younger one in return for another seven years of work.”
Gen.29.27.kjv: Fulfil her week, and we will give thee this also for the service which thou shalt serve with me yet seven other years.

Gen.29.28.bsb: And Jacob did just that. He finished the week’s celebration, and Laban gave him his daughter Rachel as his wife.
Gen.29.28.kjv: And Jacob did so, and fulfilled her week: and he gave him Rachel his daughter to wife also.

Gen.29.30.bsb: Jacob slept with Rachel as well, and indeed, he loved Rachel more than Leah. So he worked for Laban another seven years.
Gen.29.30.kjv: And he went in also unto Rachel, and he loved also Rachel more than Leah, and served with him yet seven other years.

Gen.6.18.bsb: But I will establish My covenant with you, and you will enter the ark—you and your sons and your wife and your sons’ wives with you.
Gen.6.18.kjv: But with thee will I establish my covenant; and thou shalt come into the ark, thou, and thy sons, and thy wife, and thy sons’ wives with thee.

Gen.12.7.bsb: Then the LORD appeared to Abram and said, “I will give this land to your offspring.” So Abram built an altar there to the LORD, who had appeared to him.
Gen.12.7.kjv: And the Lord appeared unto Abram, and said, Unto thy seed will I give this land: and there builded he an altar unto the Lord, who appeared unto him.

Gen.13.15.bsb: for all the land that you see, I will give to you and your offspring forever.
Gen.13.15.kjv: For all the land which thou seest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed for ever.

Gen.17.8.bsb: And to you and your descendants I will give the land where you are residing—all the land of Canaan—as an eternal possession; and I will be their God.”
Gen.17.8.kjv: And I will give unto thee, and to thy seed after thee, the land wherein thou art a stranger, all the land of Canaan, for an everlasting possession; and I will be their God.

Gen.26.3.bsb: Stay in this land as a foreigner, and I will be with you and bless you. For I will give all these lands to you and your offspring, and I will confirm the oath that I swore to your father Abraham.
Gen.26.3.kjv: Sojourn in this land, and I will be with thee, and will bless thee; for unto thee, and unto thy seed, I will give all these countries, and I will perform the oath which I sware unto Abraham thy father;

Gen.26.4.bsb: I will make your descendants as numerous as the stars in the sky, and I will give them all these lands, and through your offspring all nations of the earth will be blessed,
Gen.26.4.kjv: And I will make thy seed to multiply as the stars of heaven, and will give unto thy seed all these countries; and in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed;

Gen.26.5.bsb: because Abraham listened to My voice and kept My charge, My commandments, My statutes, and My laws.”
Gen.26.5.kjv: Because that Abraham obeyed my voice, and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws.

Gen.26.24.bsb: and that night the LORD appeared to him and said, “I am the God of your father Abraham. Do not be afraid, for I am with you. I will bless you and multiply your descendants for the sake of My servant Abraham.”
Gen.26.24.kjv: And the Lord appeared unto him the same night, and said, I am the God of Abraham thy father: fear not, for I am with thee, and will bless thee, and multiply thy seed for my servant Abraham’s sake.

Gen.17.9.bsb: God also said to Abraham, “You must keep My covenant—you and your descendants in the generations after you.
Gen.17.9.kjv: And God said unto Abraham, Thou shalt keep my covenant therefore, thou, and thy seed after thee in their generations.

Gen.17.10.bsb: This is My covenant with you and your descendants after you, which you are to keep: Every male among you must be circumcised.
Gen.17.10.kjv: This is my covenant, which ye shall keep, between me and you and thy seed after thee; Every man child among you shall be circumcised.

Gen.17.11.bsb: You are to circumcise the flesh of your foreskin, and this will be a sign of the covenant between Me and you.
Gen.17.11.kjv: And ye shall circumcise the flesh of your foreskin; and it shall be a token of the covenant betwixt me and you.

Gen.17.12.bsb: Generation after generation, every male must be circumcised when he is eight days old, including those born in your household and those purchased from a foreigner—even those who are not your offspring.
Gen.17.12.kjv: And he that is eight days old shall be circumcised among you, every man child in your generations, he that is born in the house, or bought with money of any stranger, which is not of thy seed.

Gen.17.13.bsb: Whether they are born in your household or purchased, they must be circumcised. My covenant in your flesh will be an everlasting covenant.
Gen.17.13.kjv: He that is born in thy house, and he that is bought with thy money, must needs be circumcised: and my covenant shall be in your flesh for an everlasting covenant.

Gen.17.14.bsb: But if any male is not circumcised, he will be cut off from his people; he has broken My covenant.”
Gen.17.14.kjv: And the uncircumcised man child whose flesh of his foreskin is not circumcised, that soul shall be cut off from his people; he hath broken my covenant.

Gen.4.1.bsb: And Adam had relations with his wife Eve, and she conceived and gave birth to Cain. “With the help of the LORD I have brought forth a man,” she said.
Gen.4.1.kjv: And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain, and said, I have gotten a man from the Lord.

Gen.4.25.bsb: And Adam again had relations with his wife, and she gave birth to a son and named him Seth, saying, “God has granted me another seed in place of Abel, since Cain killed him.”
Gen.4.25.kjv: And Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son, and called his name Seth: For God, said she, hath appointed me another seed instead of Abel, whom Cain slew.

Gen.17.16.bsb: And I will bless her and will surely give you a son by her. I will bless her, and she will be the mother of nations; kings of peoples will descend from her.”
