Gen.17.16.kjv: And I will bless her, and give thee a son also of her: yea, I will bless her, and she shall be a mother of nations; kings of people shall be of her.

Gen.29.32.bsb: And Leah conceived and gave birth to a son, and she named him Reuben, for she said, “The LORD has seen my affliction. Surely my husband will love me now.”
Gen.29.32.kjv: And Leah conceived, and bare a son, and she called his name Reuben: for she said, Surely the Lord hath looked upon my affliction; now therefore my husband will love me.

Gen.29.33.bsb: Again she conceived and gave birth to a son, and she said, “Because the LORD has heard that I am unloved, He has given me this son as well.” So she named him Simeon.
Gen.29.33.kjv: And she conceived again, and bare a son; and said, Because the Lord hath heard that I was hated, he hath therefore given me this son also: and she called his name Simeon.

Gen.29.34.bsb: Once again Leah conceived and gave birth to a son, and she said, “Now at last my husband will become attached to me, because I have borne him three sons.” So he was named Levi.
Gen.29.34.kjv: And she conceived again, and bare a son; and said, Now this time will my husband be joined unto me, because I have born him three sons: therefore was his name called Levi.

Gen.29.35.bsb: And once more she conceived and gave birth to a son and said, “This time I will praise the LORD.” So she named him Judah. Then Leah stopped having children.
Gen.29.35.kjv: And she conceived again, and bare a son: and she said, Now will I praise the Lord: therefore she called his name Judah; and left bearing.

Gen.30.2.bsb: Jacob became angry with Rachel and said, “Am I in the place of God, who has withheld children from you?”
Gen.30.2.kjv: And Jacob’s anger was kindled against Rachel: and he said, Am I in God’s stead, who hath withheld from thee the fruit of the womb?

Gen.30.6.bsb: Then Rachel said, “God has vindicated me; He has heard my plea and given me a son.” So she named him Dan.
Gen.30.6.kjv: And Rachel said, God hath judged me, and hath also heard my voice, and hath given me a son: therefore called she his name Dan.

Gen.33.5.bsb: When Esau looked up and saw the women and children, he asked, “Who are these with you?” Jacob answered, “These are the children God has graciously given your servant.”
Gen.33.5.kjv: And he lifted up his eyes, and saw the women and the children; and said, Who are those with thee? And he said, The children which God hath graciously given thy servant.

Gen.5.29.bsb: And he named him Noah, saying, “May this one comfort us in the labor and toil of our hands caused by the ground that the LORD has cursed.”
Gen.5.29.kjv: And he called his name Noah, saying, This same shall comfort us concerning our work and toil of our hands, because of the ground which the Lord hath cursed.

Gen.30.1.bsb: When Rachel saw that she was not bearing any children for Jacob, she envied her sister. “Give me children, or I will die!” she said to Jacob.
Gen.30.1.kjv: And when Rachel saw that she bare Jacob no children, Rachel envied her sister; and said unto Jacob, Give me children, or else I die.

Gen.7.1.bsb: Then the LORD said to Noah, “Go into the ark, you and all your family, because I have found you righteous in this generation.
Gen.7.1.kjv: And the Lord said unto Noah, Come thou and all thy house into the ark; for thee have I seen righteous before me in this generation.

Gen.46.29.bsb: Joseph prepared his chariot and went there to meet his father Israel. Joseph presented himself to him, embraced him, and wept profusely.
Gen.46.29.kjv: And Joseph made ready his chariot, and went up to meet Israel his father, to Goshen, and presented himself unto him; and he fell on his neck, and wept on his neck a good while.

Gen.28.7.bsb: and that Jacob had obeyed his father and mother and gone to Paddan-aram.
Gen.28.7.kjv: And that Jacob obeyed his father and his mother, and was gone to Padan–aram;

Gen.47.30.bsb: but when I lie down with my fathers, carry me out of Egypt and bury me with them.” Joseph answered, “I will do as you have requested.”
Gen.47.30.kjv: But I will lie with my fathers, and thou shalt carry me out of Egypt, and bury me in their buryingplace. And he said, I will do as thou hast said.

Gen.45.9.bsb: Now return quickly to my father and tell him, ‘This is what your son Joseph says: God has made me lord of all Egypt. Come down to me without delay.
Gen.45.9.kjv: Haste ye, and go up to my father, and say unto him, Thus saith thy son Joseph, God hath made me lord of all Egypt: come down unto me, tarry not:

Gen.45.10.bsb: You shall settle in the land of Goshen and be near me—you and your children and grandchildren, your flocks and herds, and everything you own.
Gen.45.10.kjv: And thou shalt dwell in the land of Goshen, and thou shalt be near unto me, thou, and thy children, and thy children’s children, and thy flocks, and thy herds, and all that thou hast:

Gen.45.11.bsb: And there I will provide for you, because there will be five more years of famine. Otherwise, you and your household and everything you own will come to destitution.’
Gen.45.11.kjv: And there will I nourish thee; for yet there are five years of famine; lest thou, and thy household, and all that thou hast, come to poverty.

Gen.47.12.bsb: Joseph also provided his father and brothers and all his father’s household with food for their families.
Gen.47.12.kjv: And Joseph nourished his father, and his brethren, and all his father’s household, with bread, according to their families.

Gen.9.23.bsb: Then Shem and Japheth took a garment and placed it across their shoulders, and walking backward, they covered their father’s nakedness. Their faces were turned away so that they did not see their father’s nakedness.
Gen.9.23.kjv: And Shem and Japheth took a garment, and laid it upon both their shoulders, and went backward, and covered the nakedness of their father; and their faces were backward, and they saw not their father’s nakedness.

Gen.22.6.bsb: Abraham took the wood for the burnt offering and placed it on his son Isaac. He himself carried the fire and the sacrificial knife, and the two of them walked on together.
Gen.22.6.kjv: And Abraham took the wood of the burnt offering, and laid it upon Isaac his son; and he took the fire in his hand, and a knife; and they went both of them together.

Gen.22.7.bsb: Then Isaac said to his father Abraham, “My father!” “Here I am, my son,” he replied. “The fire and the wood are here,” said Isaac, “but where is the lamb for the burnt offering?”
Gen.22.7.kjv: And Isaac spake unto Abraham his father, and said, My father: and he said, Here am I, my son. And he said, Behold the fire and the wood: but where is the lamb for a burnt offering?

Gen.22.8.bsb: Abraham answered, “God Himself will provide the lamb for the burnt offering, my son.” And the two walked on together.
Gen.22.8.kjv: And Abraham said, My son, God will provide himself a lamb for a burnt offering: so they went both of them together.

Gen.22.9.bsb: When they arrived at the place God had designated, Abraham built the altar there and arranged the wood. He bound his son Isaac and placed him on the altar, atop the wood.
Gen.22.9.kjv: And they came to the place which God had told him of; and Abraham built an altar there, and laid the wood in order, and bound Isaac his son, and laid him on the altar upon the wood.

Gen.22.10.bsb: Then Abraham reached out his hand and took the knife to slaughter his son.
Gen.22.10.kjv: And Abraham stretched forth his hand, and took the knife to slay his son.

Gen.28.6.bsb: Now Esau learned that Isaac had blessed Jacob and sent him to Paddan-aram to take a wife there, commanding him, “Do not marry a Canaanite woman,”
Gen.28.6.kjv: When Esau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob, and sent him away to Padan–aram, to take him a wife from thence; and that as he blessed him he gave him a charge, saying, Thou shalt not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan;

Gen.28.8.bsb: And seeing that his father Isaac disapproved of the Canaanite women,
Gen.28.8.kjv: And Esau seeing that the daughters of Canaan pleased not Isaac his father;

Gen.28.9.bsb: Esau went to Ishmael and married Mahalath, the sister of Nebaioth and daughter of Abraham’s son Ishmael, in addition to the wives he already had.
Gen.28.9.kjv: Then went Esau unto Ishmael, and took unto the wives which he had Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael Abraham’s son, the sister of Nebajoth, to be his wife.

Gen.44.18.bsb: Then Judah approached Joseph and said, “Sir, please let your servant speak personally to my lord. Do not be angry with your servant, for you are equal to Pharaoh himself.
Gen.44.18.kjv: Then Judah came near unto him, and said, Oh my lord, let thy servant, I pray thee, speak a word in my lord’s ears, and let not thine anger burn against thy servant: for thou art even as Pharaoh.

Gen.44.19.bsb: My lord asked his servants, ‘Do you have a father or a brother?’
Gen.44.19.kjv: My lord asked his servants, saying, Have ye a father, or a brother?

Gen.44.20.bsb: And we answered, ‘We have an elderly father and a younger brother, the child of his old age. The boy’s brother is dead. He is the only one of his mother’s sons left, and his father loves him.’
Gen.44.20.kjv: And we said unto my lord, We have a father, an old man, and a child of his old age, a little one; and his brother is dead, and he alone is left of his mother, and his father loveth him.

Gen.44.21.bsb: Then you told your servants, ‘Bring him down to me so that I can see him for myself.’
Gen.44.21.kjv: And thou saidst unto thy servants, Bring him down unto me, that I may set mine eyes upon him.

Gen.44.22.bsb: So we said to my lord, ‘The boy cannot leave his father. If he were to leave, his father would die.’
Gen.44.22.kjv: And we said unto my lord, The lad cannot leave his father: for if he should leave his father, his father would die.

Gen.44.23.bsb: But you said to your servants, ‘Unless your younger brother comes down with you, you will not see my face again.’
Gen.44.23.kjv: And thou saidst unto thy servants, Except your youngest brother come down with you, ye shall see my face no more.

Gen.44.24.bsb: Now when we returned to your servant my father, we relayed your words to him.
Gen.44.24.kjv: And it came to pass when we came up unto thy servant my father, we told him the words of my lord.

Gen.44.25.bsb: Then our father said, ‘Go back and buy us some food.’
Gen.44.25.kjv: And our father said, Go again, and buy us a little food.

Gen.44.26.bsb: But we answered, ‘We cannot go down there unless our younger brother goes with us. So if our younger brother is not with us, we cannot see the man.’
Gen.44.26.kjv: And we said, We cannot go down: if our youngest brother be with us, then will we go down: for we may not see the man’s face, except our youngest brother be with us.

Gen.44.27.bsb: And your servant my father said to us, ‘You know that my wife bore me two sons.
Gen.44.27.kjv: And thy servant my father said unto us, Ye know that my wife bare me two sons:

Gen.44.28.bsb: When one of them was gone, I said: “Surely he has been torn to pieces.” And I have not seen him since.
Gen.44.28.kjv: And the one went out from me, and I said, Surely he is torn in pieces; and I saw him not since:

Gen.44.29.bsb: Now if you also take this one from me and harm comes to him, you will bring my gray hair down to Sheol in sorrow.’
Gen.44.29.kjv: And if ye take this also from me, and mischief befall him, ye shall bring down my gray hairs with sorrow to the grave.

Gen.44.30.bsb: So if the boy is not with us when I return to your servant, and if my father, whose life is wrapped up in the boy’s life,
Gen.44.30.kjv: Now therefore when I come to thy servant my father, and the lad be not with us; seeing that his life is bound up in the lad’s life;

Gen.44.31.bsb: sees that the boy is not with us, he will die. Then your servants will have brought the gray hair of your servant our father down to Sheol in sorrow.
Gen.44.31.kjv: It shall come to pass, when he seeth that the lad is not with us, that he will die: and thy servants shall bring down the gray hairs of thy servant our father with sorrow to the grave.

Gen.44.32.bsb: Indeed, your servant guaranteed the boy’s safety to my father, saying, ‘If I do not return him to you, I will bear the guilt before you, my father, all my life.’
Gen.44.32.kjv: For thy servant became surety for the lad unto my father, saying, If I bring him not unto thee, then I shall bear the blame to my father for ever.

Gen.44.33.bsb: Now please let your servant stay here as my lord’s slave in place of the boy. Let him return with his brothers.
Gen.44.33.kjv: Now therefore, I pray thee, let thy servant abide instead of the lad a bondman to my lord; and let the lad go up with his brethren.

Gen.44.34.bsb: For how can I go back to my father without the boy? I could not bear to see the misery that would overwhelm him.”
Gen.44.34.kjv: For how shall I go up to my father, and the lad be not with me? lest peradventure I see the evil that shall come on my father.

Gen.45.12.bsb: Behold! You and my brother Benjamin can see that I, Joseph, am the one speaking with you.
Gen.45.12.kjv: And, behold, your eyes see, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin, that it is my mouth that speaketh unto you.

Gen.45.13.bsb: Tell my father about all my splendor in Egypt and everything you have seen. And bring my father down here quickly.”
Gen.45.13.kjv: And ye shall tell my father of all my glory in Egypt, and of all that ye have seen; and ye shall haste and bring down my father hither.

Gen.47.11.bsb: So Joseph settled his father and brothers in the land of Egypt and gave them property in the best part of the land, the district of Rameses, as Pharaoh had commanded.
Gen.47.11.kjv: And Joseph placed his father and his brethren, and gave them a possession in the land of Egypt, in the best of the land, in the land of Rameses, as Pharaoh had commanded.

Gen.50.1.bsb: Then Joseph fell upon his father’s face, wept over him, and kissed him.
Gen.50.1.kjv: And Joseph fell upon his father’s face, and wept upon him, and kissed him.

Gen.50.2.bsb: And Joseph directed the physicians in his service to embalm his father Israel. So they embalmed him,
Gen.50.2.kjv: And Joseph commanded his servants the physicians to embalm his father: and the physicians embalmed Israel.

Gen.50.3.bsb: taking the forty days required to complete the embalming. And the Egyptians mourned for him seventy days.
Gen.50.3.kjv: And forty days were fulfilled for him; for so are fulfilled the days of those which are embalmed: and the Egyptians mourned for him threescore and ten days.

Gen.50.4.bsb: When the days of mourning had passed, Joseph said to Pharaoh’s court, “If I have found favor in your eyes, please tell Pharaoh that
Gen.50.4.kjv: And when the days of his mourning were past, Joseph spake unto the house of Pharaoh, saying, If now I have found grace in your eyes, speak, I pray you, in the ears of Pharaoh, saying,

Gen.50.5.bsb: my father made me swear an oath when he said, ‘I am about to die. You must bury me in the tomb that I dug for myself in the land of Canaan.’ Now let me go and bury my father, and then return.”
Gen.50.5.kjv: My father made me swear, saying, Lo, I die: in my grave which I have digged for me in the land of Canaan, there shalt thou bury me. Now therefore let me go up, I pray thee, and bury my father, and I will come again.

Gen.50.6.bsb: Pharaoh replied, “Go up and bury your father, as he made you swear to do.”
Gen.50.6.kjv: And Pharaoh said, Go up, and bury thy father, according as he made thee swear.

Gen.50.7.bsb: Then Joseph went to bury his father, and all the servants of Pharaoh accompanied him—the elders of Pharaoh’s household and all the elders of the land of Egypt—
Gen.50.7.kjv: And Joseph went up to bury his father: and with him went up all the servants of Pharaoh, the elders of his house, and all the elders of the land of Egypt,

Gen.50.8.bsb: along with all of Joseph’s household, and his brothers, and his father’s household. Only their children and flocks and herds were left in Goshen.
Gen.50.8.kjv: And all the house of Joseph, and his brethren, and his father’s house: only their little ones, and their flocks, and their herds, they left in the land of Goshen.

Gen.50.9.bsb: Chariots and horsemen alike went up with him, and it was an exceedingly large procession.
Gen.50.9.kjv: And there went up with him both chariots and horsemen: and it was a very great company.

Gen.50.10.bsb: When they reached the threshing floor of Atad, which is across the Jordan, they lamented and wailed loudly, and Joseph mourned for his father seven days.
Gen.50.10.kjv: And they came to the threshingfloor of Atad, which is beyond Jordan, and there they mourned with a great and very sore lamentation: and he made a mourning for his father seven days.

Gen.50.11.bsb: When the Canaanites of the land saw the mourning at the threshing floor of Atad, they said, “This is a solemn ceremony of mourning by the Egyptians.” Thus the place across the Jordan is called Abel-mizraim.
Gen.50.11.kjv: And when the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites, saw the mourning in the floor of Atad, they said, This is a grievous mourning to the Egyptians: wherefore the name of it was called Abel–mizraim, which is beyond Jordan.

Gen.50.12.bsb: So Jacob’s sons did as he had charged them.
Gen.50.12.kjv: And his sons did unto him according as he commanded them:

Gen.50.13.bsb: They carried him to the land of Canaan and buried him in the cave at Machpelah in the field near Mamre, which Abraham had purchased from Ephron the Hittite as a burial site.
Gen.50.13.kjv: For his sons carried him into the land of Canaan, and buried him in the cave of the field of Machpelah, which Abraham bought with the field for a possession of a buryingplace of Ephron the Hittite, before Mamre.

Gen.19.30.bsb: Lot and his two daughters left Zoar and settled in the mountains—for he was afraid to stay in Zoar—where they lived in a cave.
Gen.19.30.kjv: And Lot went up out of Zoar, and dwelt in the mountain, and his two daughters with him; for he feared to dwell in Zoar: and he dwelt in a cave, he and his two daughters.

Gen.19.31.bsb: One day the older daughter said to the younger, “Our father is old, and there is no man in the land to sleep with us, as is the custom over all the earth.
Gen.19.31.kjv: And the firstborn said unto the younger, Our father is old, and there is not a man in the earth to come in unto us after the manner of all the earth:

Gen.19.32.bsb: Come, let us get our father drunk with wine so we can sleep with him and preserve his line.”
Gen.19.32.kjv: Come, let us make our father drink wine, and we will lie with him, that we may preserve seed of our father.

Gen.19.33.bsb: So that night they got their father drunk with wine, and the firstborn went in and slept with her father; he was not aware when she lay down or when she got up.
Gen.19.33.kjv: And they made their father drink wine that night: and the firstborn went in, and lay with her father; and he perceived not when she lay down, nor when she arose.

Gen.19.34.bsb: The next day the older daughter said to the younger, “Look, I slept with my father last night. Let us get him drunk with wine again tonight so you can go in and sleep with him and we can preserve our father’s line.”
Gen.19.34.kjv: And it came to pass on the morrow, that the firstborn said unto the younger, Behold, I lay yesternight with my father: let us make him drink wine this night also; and go thou in, and lie with him, that we may preserve seed of our father.

Gen.19.35.bsb: So again that night they got their father drunk with wine, and the younger daughter went in and slept with him; he was not aware when she lay down or when she got up.
Gen.19.35.kjv: And they made their father drink wine that night also: and the younger arose, and lay with him; and he perceived not when she lay down, nor when she arose.

Gen.19.36.bsb: Thus both of Lot’s daughters became pregnant by their father.
Gen.19.36.kjv: Thus were both the daughters of Lot with child by their father.

Gen.19.37.bsb: The older daughter gave birth to a son and named him Moab. He is the father of the Moabites of today.
Gen.19.37.kjv: And the firstborn bare a son, and called his name Moab: the same is the father of the Moabites unto this day.

Gen.19.38.bsb: The younger daughter also gave birth to a son, and she named him Ben-ammi. He is the father of the Ammonites of today.
Gen.19.38.kjv: And the younger, she also bare a son, and called his name Ben–ammi: the same is the father of the children of Ammon unto this day.

Gen.28.17.bsb: And he was afraid and said, “How awesome is this place! This is none other than the house of God; this is the gate of heaven!”
Gen.28.17.kjv: And he was afraid, and said, How dreadful is this place! this is none other but the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven.

Gen.12.3.bsb: I will bless those who bless you and curse those who curse you; and all the families of the earth will be blessed through you.”
Gen.12.3.kjv: And I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee: and in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed.

Gen.4.4.bsb: while Abel brought the best portions of the firstborn of his flock. And the LORD looked with favor on Abel and his offering,
Gen.4.4.kjv: And Abel, he also brought of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof. And the Lord had respect unto Abel and to his offering:

Gen.21.27.bsb: So Abraham brought sheep and cattle and gave them to Abimelech, and the two men made a covenant.
Gen.21.27.kjv: And Abraham took sheep and oxen, and gave them unto Abimelech; and both of them made a covenant.

Gen.21.28.bsb: Abraham separated seven ewe lambs from the flock,
Gen.21.28.kjv: And Abraham set seven ewe lambs of the flock by themselves.

Gen.21.29.bsb: and Abimelech asked him, “Why have you set apart these seven ewe lambs?”
Gen.21.29.kjv: And Abimelech said unto Abraham, What mean these seven ewe lambs which thou hast set by themselves?

Gen.21.30.bsb: He replied, “You are to accept the seven ewe lambs from my hand as my witness that I dug this well.”
Gen.21.30.kjv: And he said, For these seven ewe lambs shalt thou take of my hand, that they may be a witness unto me, that I have digged this well.

Gen.26.30.bsb: So Isaac prepared a feast for them, and they ate and drank.
Gen.26.30.kjv: And he made them a feast, and they did eat and drink.

Gen.31.45.bsb: So Jacob picked out a stone and set it up as a pillar,
Gen.31.45.kjv: And Jacob took a stone, and set it up for a pillar.

Gen.31.46.bsb: and he said to his relatives, “Gather some stones.” So they took stones and made a mound, and there by the mound they ate.
Gen.31.46.kjv: And Jacob said unto his brethren, Gather stones; and they took stones, and made an heap: and they did eat there upon the heap.

Gen.31.49.bsb: It was also called Mizpah, because Laban said, “May the LORD keep watch between you and me when we are absent from each other.
Gen.31.49.kjv: And Mizpah; for he said, The Lord watch between me and thee, when we are absent one from another.

Gen.31.50.bsb: If you mistreat my daughters or take other wives, although no one is with us, remember that God is a witness between you and me.”
Gen.31.50.kjv: If thou shalt afflict my daughters, or if thou shalt take other wives beside my daughters, no man is with us; see, God is witness betwixt me and thee.

Gen.31.51.bsb: Laban also said to Jacob, “Here is the mound, and here is the pillar I have set up between you and me.
Gen.31.51.kjv: And Laban said to Jacob, Behold this heap, and behold this pillar, which I have cast betwixt me and thee;

Gen.31.52.bsb: This mound is a witness, and this pillar is a witness, that I will not go past this mound to harm you, and you will not go past this mound and pillar to harm me.
Gen.31.52.kjv: This heap be witness, and this pillar be witness, that I will not pass over this heap to thee, and that thou shalt not pass over this heap and this pillar unto me, for harm.

Gen.31.53.bsb: May the God of Abraham and the God of Nahor, the God of their father, judge between us.” So Jacob swore by the Fear of his father Isaac.
Gen.31.53.kjv: The God of Abraham, and the God of Nahor, the God of their father, judge betwixt us. And Jacob sware by the fear of his father Isaac.

Gen.15.9.bsb: And the LORD said to him, “Bring Me a heifer, a goat, and a ram, each three years old, along with a turtledove and a young pigeon.”
Gen.15.9.kjv: And he said unto him, Take me an heifer of three years old, and a she goat of three years old, and a ram of three years old, and a turtledove, and a young pigeon.

Gen.15.10.bsb: So Abram brought all these to Him, split each of them down the middle, and laid the halves opposite each other. The birds, however, he did not cut in half.
Gen.15.10.kjv: And he took unto him all these, and divided them in the midst, and laid each piece one against another: but the birds divided he not.

Gen.15.11.bsb: And the birds of prey descended on the carcasses, but Abram drove them away.
Gen.15.11.kjv: And when the fowls came down upon the carcases, Abram drove them away.

Gen.15.12.bsb: As the sun was setting, Abram fell into a deep sleep, and suddenly great terror and darkness overwhelmed him.
Gen.15.12.kjv: And when the sun was going down, a deep sleep fell upon Abram; and, lo, an horror of great darkness fell upon him.

Gen.15.13.bsb: Then the LORD said to Abram, “Know for certain that your descendants will be strangers in a land that is not their own, and they will be enslaved and mistreated four hundred years.
Gen.15.13.kjv: And he said unto Abram, Know of a surety that thy seed shall be a stranger in a land that is not theirs, and shall serve them; and they shall afflict them four hundred years;

Gen.15.14.bsb: But I will judge the nation they serve as slaves, and afterward they will depart with many possessions.
Gen.15.14.kjv: And also that nation, whom they shall serve, will I judge: and afterward shall they come out with great substance.

Gen.15.15.bsb: You, however, will go to your fathers in peace and be buried at a ripe old age.
Gen.15.15.kjv: And thou shalt go to thy fathers in peace; thou shalt be buried in a good old age.

Gen.15.16.bsb: In the fourth generation your descendants will return here, for the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet complete.”
Gen.15.16.kjv: But in the fourth generation they shall come hither again: for the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet full.

Gen.15.17.bsb: When the sun had set and darkness had fallen, behold, a smoking firepot and a flaming torch appeared and passed between the halves of the carcasses.
Gen.15.17.kjv: And it came to pass, that, when the sun went down, and it was dark, behold a smoking furnace, and a burning lamp that passed between those pieces.

Gen.21.26.bsb: Abimelech replied, “I do not know who has done this. You did not tell me, so I have not heard about it until today.”
Gen.21.26.kjv: And Abimelech said, I wot not who hath done this thing: neither didst thou tell me, neither yet heard I of it, but to day.

Gen.21.31.bsb: So that place was called Beersheba, because it was there that the two of them swore an oath.
Gen.21.31.kjv: Wherefore he called that place Beer–sheba; because there they sware both of them.

Gen.21.32.bsb: After they had made the covenant at Beersheba, Abimelech and Phicol the commander of his army got up and returned to the land of the Philistines.
Gen.21.32.kjv: Thus they made a covenant at Beer–sheba: then Abimelech rose up, and Phichol the chief captain of his host, and they returned into the land of the Philistines.

Gen.26.26.bsb: Later, Abimelech came to Isaac from Gerar, with Ahuzzath his adviser and Phicol the commander of his army.
Gen.26.26.kjv: Then Abimelech went to him from Gerar, and Ahuzzath one of his friends, and Phichol the chief captain of his army.

Gen.26.27.bsb: “Why have you come to me?” Isaac asked them. “You hated me and sent me away.”
Gen.26.27.kjv: And Isaac said unto them, Wherefore come ye to me, seeing ye hate me, and have sent me away from you?

Gen.26.28.bsb: “We can plainly see that the LORD has been with you,” they replied. “We recommend that there should now be an oath between us and you. Let us make a covenant with you
Gen.26.28.kjv: And they said, We saw certainly that the Lord was with thee: and we said, Let there be now an oath betwixt us, even betwixt us and thee, and let us make a covenant with thee;

Gen.26.29.bsb: that you will not harm us, just as we have not harmed you but have done only good to you, sending you on your way in peace. And now you are blessed by the LORD.”
Gen.26.29.kjv: That thou wilt do us no hurt, as we have not touched thee, and as we have done unto thee nothing but good, and have sent thee away in peace: thou art now the blessed of the Lord.

Gen.26.31.bsb: And they got up early the next morning and swore an oath to each other. Then Isaac sent them on their way, and they left him in peace.
Gen.26.31.kjv: And they rose up betimes in the morning, and sware one to another: and Isaac sent them away, and they departed from him in peace.

Gen.31.44.bsb: Come now, let us make a covenant, you and I, and let it serve as a witness between you and me.”
Gen.31.44.kjv: Now therefore come thou, let us make a covenant, I and thou; and let it be for a witness between me and thee.

Gen.31.47.bsb: Laban called it Jegar-sahadutha, and Jacob called it Galeed.
Gen.31.47.kjv: And Laban called it Jegar–sahadutha: but Jacob called it Galeed.

Gen.31.48.bsb: Then Laban declared, “This mound is a witness between you and me this day.” Therefore the place was called Galeed.
Gen.31.48.kjv: And Laban said, This heap is a witness between me and thee this day. Therefore was the name of it called Galeed;

Gen.31.54.bsb: Then Jacob offered a sacrifice on the mountain and invited his relatives to eat a meal. And after they had eaten, they spent the night on the mountain.
Gen.31.54.kjv: Then Jacob offered sacrifice upon the mount, and called his brethren to eat bread: and they did eat bread, and tarried all night in the mount.

Gen.50.24.bsb: Then Joseph said to his brothers, “I am about to die, but God will surely visit you and bring you up from this land to the land He promised on oath to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.”
Gen.50.24.kjv: And Joseph said unto his brethren, I die: and God will surely visit you, and bring you out of this land unto the land which he sware to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.

Gen.8.20.bsb: Then Noah built an altar to the LORD. And taking from every kind of clean animal and clean bird, he offered burnt offerings on the altar.
Gen.8.20.kjv: And Noah builded an altar unto the Lord; and took of every clean beast, and of every clean fowl, and offered burnt offerings on the altar.

Gen.8.22.bsb: As long as the earth endures, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night shall never cease.”
Gen.8.22.kjv: While the earth remaineth, seedtime and harvest, and cold and heat, and summer and winter, and day and night shall not cease.

Gen.9.4.bsb: But you must not eat meat with its lifeblood still in it.
Gen.9.4.kjv: But flesh with the life thereof, which is the blood thereof, shall ye not eat.

Gen.9.5.bsb: And surely I will require the life of any man or beast by whose hand your lifeblood is shed. I will demand an accounting from anyone who takes the life of his fellow man:
Gen.9.5.kjv: And surely your blood of your lives will I require; at the hand of every beast will I require it, and at the hand of man; at the hand of every man’s brother will I require the life of man.

Gen.9.7.bsb: But as for you, be fruitful and multiply; spread out across the earth and multiply upon it.”
Gen.9.7.kjv: And you, be ye fruitful, and multiply; bring forth abundantly in the earth, and multiply therein.

Gen.9.8.bsb: Then God said to Noah and his sons with him,
Gen.9.8.kjv: And God spake unto Noah, and to his sons with him, saying,

Gen.9.9.bsb: “Behold, I now establish My covenant with you and your descendants after you,
Gen.9.9.kjv: And I, behold, I establish my covenant with you, and with your seed after you;

Gen.9.10.bsb: and with every living creature that was with you—the birds, the livestock, and every beast of the earth—every living thing that came out of the ark.
Gen.9.10.kjv: And with every living creature that is with you, of the fowl, of the cattle, and of every beast of the earth with you; from all that go out of the ark, to every beast of the earth.

Gen.9.11.bsb: And I establish My covenant with you: Never again will all life be cut off by the waters of a flood; never again will there be a flood to destroy the earth.”
Gen.9.11.kjv: And I will establish my covenant with you; neither shall all flesh be cut off any more by the waters of a flood; neither shall there any more be a flood to destroy the earth.

Gen.9.12.bsb: And God said, “This is the sign of the covenant I am making between Me and you and every living creature with you, a covenant for all generations to come:
Gen.9.12.kjv: And God said, This is the token of the covenant which I make between me and you and every living creature that is with you, for perpetual generations:

Gen.9.13.bsb: I have set My rainbow in the clouds, and it will be a sign of the covenant between Me and the earth.
Gen.9.13.kjv: I do set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a token of a covenant between me and the earth.

Gen.9.14.bsb: Whenever I form clouds over the earth and the rainbow appears in the clouds,
Gen.9.14.kjv: And it shall come to pass, when I bring a cloud over the earth, that the bow shall be seen in the cloud:

Gen.9.15.bsb: I will remember My covenant between Me and you and every living creature of every kind. Never again will the waters become a flood to destroy all life.
Gen.9.15.kjv: And I will remember my covenant, which is between me and you and every living creature of all flesh; and the waters shall no more become a flood to destroy all flesh.

Gen.9.17.bsb: So God said to Noah, “This is the sign of the covenant that I have established between Me and every creature on the earth.”
Gen.9.17.kjv: And God said unto Noah, This is the token of the covenant, which I have established between me and all flesh that is upon the earth.

Gen.8.16.bsb: “Come out of the ark, you and your wife, along with your sons and their wives.
Gen.8.16.kjv: Go forth of the ark, thou, and thy wife, and thy sons, and thy sons’ wives with thee.

Gen.12.1.bsb: Then the LORD said to Abram, “Leave your country, your kindred, and your father’s household, and go to the land I will show you.
Gen.12.1.kjv: Now the Lord had said unto Abram, Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father’s house, unto a land that I will shew thee:

Gen.12.2.bsb: I will make you into a great nation, and I will bless you; I will make your name great, so that you will be a blessing.
Gen.12.2.kjv: And I will make of thee a great nation, and I will bless thee, and make thy name great; and thou shalt be a blessing:

Gen.17.1.bsb: When Abram was ninety-nine years old, the LORD appeared to him and said, “I am God Almighty. Walk before Me and be blameless.
Gen.17.1.kjv: And when Abram was ninety years old and nine, the Lord appeared to Abram, and said unto him, I am the Almighty God; walk before me, and be thou perfect.

Gen.17.2.bsb: I will establish My covenant between Me and you, and I will multiply you exceedingly.”
Gen.17.2.kjv: And I will make my covenant between me and thee, and will multiply thee exceedingly.

Gen.17.3.bsb: Then Abram fell facedown, and God said to him,
Gen.17.3.kjv: And Abram fell on his face: and God talked with him, saying,

Gen.17.4.bsb: “As for Me, this is My covenant with you: You will be the father of many nations.
Gen.17.4.kjv: As for me, behold, my covenant is with thee, and thou shalt be a father of many nations.

Gen.17.5.bsb: No longer will you be called Abram, but your name will be Abraham, for I have made you a father of many nations.
Gen.17.5.kjv: Neither shall thy name any more be called Abram, but thy name shall be Abraham; for a father of many nations have I made thee.

Gen.17.6.bsb: I will make you exceedingly fruitful; I will make nations of you, and kings will descend from you.
Gen.17.6.kjv: And I will make thee exceeding fruitful, and I will make nations of thee, and kings shall come out of thee.

Gen.17.15.bsb: Then God said to Abraham, “As for Sarai your wife, do not call her Sarai, for her name is to be Sarah.
Gen.17.15.kjv: And God said unto Abraham, As for Sarai thy wife, thou shalt not call her name Sarai, but Sarah shall her name be.

Gen.17.17.bsb: Abraham fell facedown. Then he laughed and said to himself, “Can a child be born to a man who is a hundred years old? Can Sarah give birth at the age of ninety?”
Gen.17.17.kjv: Then Abraham fell upon his face, and laughed, and said in his heart, Shall a child be born unto him that is an hundred years old? and shall Sarah, that is ninety years old, bear?

Gen.17.19.bsb: But God replied, “Your wife Sarah will indeed bear you a son, and you are to name him Isaac. I will establish My covenant with him as an everlasting covenant for his descendants after him.
Gen.17.19.kjv: And God said, Sarah thy wife shall bear thee a son indeed; and thou shalt call his name Isaac: and I will establish my covenant with him for an everlasting covenant, and with his seed after him.

Gen.17.21.bsb: But I will establish My covenant with Isaac, whom Sarah will bear to you at this time next year.”
Gen.17.21.kjv: But my covenant will I establish with Isaac, which Sarah shall bear unto thee at this set time in the next year.

Gen.17.22.bsb: When He had finished speaking with Abraham, God went up from him.
Gen.17.22.kjv: And he left off talking with him, and God went up from Abraham.

Gen.28.14.bsb: Your descendants will be like the dust of the earth, and you will spread out to the west and east and north and south. All the families of the earth will be blessed through you and your offspring.
Gen.28.14.kjv: And thy seed shall be as the dust of the earth, and thou shalt spread abroad to the west, and to the east, and to the north, and to the south: and in thee and in thy seed shall all the families of the earth be blessed.

Gen.28.15.bsb: Look, I am with you, and I will watch over you wherever you go, and I will bring you back to this land. For I will not leave you until I have done what I have promised you.”
Gen.28.15.kjv: And, behold, I am with thee, and will keep thee in all places whither thou goest, and will bring thee again into this land; for I will not leave thee, until I have done that which I have spoken to thee of.

Gen.25.8.bsb: And at a ripe old age he breathed his last and died, old and contented, and was gathered to his people.
Gen.25.8.kjv: Then Abraham gave up the ghost, and died in a good old age, an old man, and full of years; and was gathered to his people.

Gen.35.29.bsb: Then he breathed his last and died and was gathered to his people, old and full of years. And his sons Esau and Jacob buried him.
Gen.35.29.kjv: And Isaac gave up the ghost, and died, and was gathered unto his people, being old and full of days: and his sons Esau and Jacob buried him.

Gen.49.33.bsb: When Jacob had finished instructing his sons, he pulled his feet into the bed and breathed his last, and he was gathered to his people.
Gen.49.33.kjv: And when Jacob had made an end of commanding his sons, he gathered up his feet into the bed, and yielded up the ghost, and was gathered unto his people.

Gen.6.7.bsb: So the LORD said, “I will blot out man, whom I have created, from the face of the earth—every man and beast and crawling creature and bird of the air—for I am grieved that I have made them.”
Gen.6.7.kjv: And the Lord said, I will destroy man whom I have created from the face of the earth; both man, and beast, and the creeping thing, and the fowls of the air; for it repenteth me that I have made them.

Gen.6.11.bsb: Now the earth was corrupt in the sight of God, and full of violence.
Gen.6.11.kjv: The earth also was corrupt before God, and the earth was filled with violence.

Gen.6.13.bsb: Then God said to Noah, “The end of all living creatures has come before Me, because through them the earth is full of violence. Now behold, I will destroy both them and the earth.
Gen.6.13.kjv: And God said unto Noah, The end of all flesh is come before me; for the earth is filled with violence through them; and, behold, I will destroy them with the earth.

Gen.27.2.bsb: “Look,” said Isaac, “I am now old, and I do not know the day of my death.
Gen.27.2.kjv: And he said, Behold now, I am old, I know not the day of my death:

Gen.27.3.bsb: Take your weapons—your quiver and bow—and go out into the field to hunt some game for me.
Gen.27.3.kjv: Now therefore take, I pray thee, thy weapons, thy quiver and thy bow, and go out to the field, and take me some venison;

Gen.27.4.bsb: Then prepare a tasty dish that I love and bring it to me to eat, so that I may bless you before I die.”
Gen.27.4.kjv: And make me savoury meat, such as I love, and bring it to me, that I may eat; that my soul may bless thee before I die.

Gen.27.22.bsb: So Jacob came close to his father Isaac, who touched him and said, “The voice is the voice of Jacob, but the hands are the hands of Esau.”
Gen.27.22.kjv: And Jacob went near unto Isaac his father; and he felt him, and said, The voice is Jacob’s voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau.

Gen.27.30.bsb: As soon as Isaac had finished blessing him and Jacob had left his father’s presence, his brother Esau returned from the hunt.
Gen.27.30.kjv: And it came to pass, as soon as Isaac had made an end of blessing Jacob, and Jacob was yet scarce gone out from the presence of Isaac his father, that Esau his brother came in from his hunting.

Gen.27.31.bsb: He too made some tasty food, brought it to his father, and said to him, “My father, sit up and eat of your son’s game, so that you may bless me.”
Gen.27.31.kjv: And he also had made savoury meat, and brought it unto his father, and said unto his father, Let my father arise, and eat of his son’s venison, that thy soul may bless me.

Gen.27.32.bsb: But his father Isaac replied, “Who are you?” “I am Esau, your firstborn son,” he answered.
Gen.27.32.kjv: And Isaac his father said unto him, Who art thou? And he said, I am thy son, thy firstborn Esau.

Gen.27.33.bsb: Isaac began to tremble violently and said, “Who was it, then, who hunted the game and brought it to me? Before you came in, I ate it all and blessed him—and indeed, he will be blessed!”
Gen.27.33.kjv: And Isaac trembled very exceedingly, and said, Who? where is he that hath taken venison, and brought it me, and I have eaten of all before thou camest, and have blessed him? yea, and he shall be blessed.

Gen.27.34.bsb: When Esau heard his father’s words, he let out a loud and bitter cry and said to his father, “Bless me too, O my father!”
Gen.27.34.kjv: And when Esau heard the words of his father, he cried with a great and exceeding bitter cry, and said unto his father, Bless me, even me also, O my father.

Gen.27.35.bsb: But Isaac replied, “Your brother came deceitfully and took your blessing.”
Gen.27.35.kjv: And he said, Thy brother came with subtilty, and hath taken away thy blessing.

Gen.27.36.bsb: So Esau declared, “Is he not rightly named Jacob? For he has cheated me twice. He took my birthright, and now he has taken my blessing.” Then he asked, “Haven’t you saved a blessing for me?”
Gen.27.36.kjv: And he said, Is not he rightly named Jacob? for he hath supplanted me these two times: he took away my birthright; and, behold, now he hath taken away my blessing. And he said, Hast thou not reserved a blessing for me?

Gen.27.38.bsb: Esau said to his father, “Do you have only one blessing, my father? Bless me too, O my father!” Then Esau wept aloud.
Gen.27.38.kjv: And Esau said unto his father, Hast thou but one blessing, my father? bless me, even me also, O my father. And Esau lifted up his voice, and wept.

Gen.49.2.bsb: Come together and listen, O sons of Jacob; listen to your father Israel.
Gen.49.2.kjv: Gather yourselves together, and hear, ye sons of Jacob; and hearken unto Israel your father.

Gen.49.3.bsb: Reuben, you are my firstborn, my might, and the beginning of my strength, excelling in honor, excelling in power.
Gen.49.3.kjv: Reuben, thou art my firstborn, my might, and the beginning of my strength, the excellency of dignity, and the excellency of power:

Gen.49.4.bsb: Uncontrolled as the waters, you will no longer excel, because you went up to your father’s bed, onto my couch, and defiled it.
Gen.49.4.kjv: Unstable as water, thou shalt not excel; because thou wentest up to thy father’s bed; then defiledst thou it: he went up to my couch.

Gen.49.8.bsb: Judah, your brothers shall praise you. Your hand shall be on the necks of your enemies; your father’s sons shall bow down to you.
Gen.49.8.kjv: Judah, thou art he whom thy brethren shall praise: thy hand shall be in the neck of thine enemies; thy father’s children shall bow down before thee.

Gen.49.9.bsb: Judah is a young lion—my son, you return from the prey. Like a lion he crouches and lies down; like a lioness, who dares to rouse him?
Gen.49.9.kjv: Judah is a lion’s whelp: from the prey, my son, thou art gone up: he stooped down, he couched as a lion, and as an old lion; who shall rouse him up?

Gen.49.11.bsb: He ties his donkey to the vine, his colt to the choicest branch. He washes his garments in wine, his robes in the blood of grapes.
Gen.49.11.kjv: Binding his foal unto the vine, and his ass’s colt unto the choice vine; he washed his garments in wine, and his clothes in the blood of grapes:

Gen.49.12.bsb: His eyes are darker than wine, and his teeth are whiter than milk.
Gen.49.12.kjv: His eyes shall be red with wine, and his teeth white with milk.

Gen.49.13.bsb: Zebulun shall dwell by the seashore and become a harbor for ships; his border shall extend to Sidon.
Gen.49.13.kjv: Zebulun shall dwell at the haven of the sea; and he shall be for an haven of ships; and his border shall be unto Zidon.

Gen.49.14.bsb: Issachar is a strong donkey, lying down between the sheepfolds.
Gen.49.14.kjv: Issachar is a strong ass couching down between two burdens:

Gen.49.15.bsb: He saw that his resting place was good and that his land was pleasant, so he bent his shoulder to the burden and submitted to labor as a servant.
Gen.49.15.kjv: And he saw that rest was good, and the land that it was pleasant; and bowed his shoulder to bear, and became a servant unto tribute.

Gen.49.16.bsb: Dan shall provide justice for his people as one of the tribes of Israel.
Gen.49.16.kjv: Dan shall judge his people, as one of the tribes of Israel.

Gen.49.17.bsb: He will be a snake by the road, a viper in the path that bites the horse’s heels so that its rider tumbles backward.
Gen.49.17.kjv: Dan shall be a serpent by the way, an adder in the path, that biteth the horse heels, so that his rider shall fall backward.

Gen.49.18.bsb: I await Your salvation, O LORD.
Gen.49.18.kjv: I have waited for thy salvation, O Lord.

Gen.49.19.bsb: Gad will be attacked by raiders, but he will attack their heels.
Gen.49.19.kjv: Gad, a troop shall overcome him: but he shall overcome at the last.

Gen.49.20.bsb: Asher’s food will be rich; he shall provide royal delicacies.
Gen.49.20.kjv: Out of Asher his bread shall be fat, and he shall yield royal dainties.

Gen.49.21.bsb: Naphtali is a doe set free that bears beautiful fawns.
Gen.49.21.kjv: Naphtali is a hind let loose: he giveth goodly words.

Gen.49.22.bsb: Joseph is a fruitful vine—a fruitful vine by a spring, whose branches scale the wall.
Gen.49.22.kjv: Joseph is a fruitful bough, even a fruitful bough by a well; whose branches run over the wall:

Gen.49.23.bsb: The archers attacked him with bitterness; they aimed at him in hostility.
Gen.49.23.kjv: The archers have sorely grieved him, and shot at him, and hated him:

Gen.49.24.bsb: Yet he steadied his bow, and his strong arms were tempered by the hands of the Mighty One of Jacob, in the name of the Shepherd, the Rock of Israel,
Gen.49.24.kjv: But his bow abode in strength, and the arms of his hands were made strong by the hands of the mighty God of Jacob; (from thence is the shepherd, the stone of Israel:)

Gen.49.25.bsb: by the God of your father who helps you, and by the Almighty who blesses you, with blessings of the heavens above, with blessings of the depths below, with blessings of the breasts and womb.
Gen.49.25.kjv: Even by the God of thy father, who shall help thee; and by the Almighty, who shall bless thee with blessings of heaven above, blessings of the deep that lieth under, blessings of the breasts, and of the womb:

Gen.49.27.bsb: Benjamin is a ravenous wolf; in the morning he devours the prey, in the evening he divides the plunder.”
Gen.49.27.kjv: Benjamin shall ravin as a wolf: in the morning he shall devour the prey, and at night he shall divide the spoil.

Gen.49.28.bsb: These are the tribes of Israel, twelve in all, and this was what their father said to them. He blessed them, and he blessed each one with a suitable blessing.
Gen.49.28.kjv: All these are the twelve tribes of Israel: and this is it that their father spake unto them, and blessed them; every one according to his blessing he blessed them.

Gen.49.29.bsb: Then Jacob instructed them, “I am about to be gathered to my people. Bury me with my fathers in the cave in the field of Ephron the Hittite.
Gen.49.29.kjv: And he charged them, and said unto them, I am to be gathered unto my people: bury me with my fathers in the cave that is in the field of Ephron the Hittite,

Gen.49.30.bsb: The cave is in the field of Machpelah near Mamre, in the land of Canaan. This is the field Abraham purchased from Ephron the Hittite as a burial site.
Gen.49.30.kjv: In the cave that is in the field of Machpelah, which is before Mamre, in the land of Canaan, which Abraham bought with the field of Ephron the Hittite for a possession of a buryingplace.

Gen.49.31.bsb: There Abraham and his wife Sarah are buried, there Isaac and his wife Rebekah are buried, and there I buried Leah.
Gen.49.31.kjv: There they buried Abraham and Sarah his wife; there they buried Isaac and Rebekah his wife; and there I buried Leah.

Gen.49.32.bsb: The field and the cave that is in it were purchased from the Hittites.”
Gen.49.32.kjv: The purchase of the field and of the cave that is therein was from the children of Heth.

Gen.16.5.bsb: Then Sarai said to Abram, “May the wrong done to me be upon you! I delivered my servant into your arms, and ever since she saw that she was pregnant, she has treated me with contempt. May the LORD judge between you and me.”
Gen.16.5.kjv: And Sarai said unto Abram, My wrong be upon thee: I have given my maid into thy bosom; and when she saw that she had conceived, I was despised in her eyes: the Lord judge between me and thee.

Gen.16.6.bsb: “Here,” said Abram, “your servant is in your hands. Do whatever you want with her.” Then Sarai treated Hagar so harshly that she fled from her.
Gen.16.6.kjv: But Abram said unto Sarai, Behold, thy maid is in thy hand; do to her as it pleaseth thee. And when Sarai dealt hardly with her, she fled from her face.

Gen.26.14.bsb: He owned so many flocks and herds and servants that the Philistines envied him.
Gen.26.14.kjv: For he had possession of flocks, and possession of herds, and great store of servants: and the Philistines envied him.

Gen.30.15.bsb: But Leah replied, “Is it not enough that you have taken away my husband? Now you want to take my son’s mandrakes as well?” “Very well,” said Rachel, “he may sleep with you tonight in exchange for your son’s mandrakes.”
Gen.30.15.kjv: And she said unto her, Is it a small matter that thou hast taken my husband? and wouldest thou take away my son’s mandrakes also? And Rachel said, Therefore he shall lie with thee to night for thy son’s mandrakes.

Gen.31.1.bsb: Now Jacob heard that Laban’s sons were saying, “Jacob has taken away all that belonged to our father and built all this wealth at our father’s expense.”
Gen.31.1.kjv: And he heard the words of Laban’s sons, saying, Jacob hath taken away all that was our father’s; and of that which was our father’s hath he gotten all this glory.

Gen.37.5.bsb: Then Joseph had a dream, and when he told it to his brothers, they hated him even more.
Gen.37.5.kjv: And Joseph dreamed a dream, and he told it his brethren: and they hated him yet the more.

Gen.37.6.bsb: He said to them, “Listen to this dream I had:
Gen.37.6.kjv: And he said unto them, Hear, I pray you, this dream which I have dreamed:

Gen.37.7.bsb: We were binding sheaves of grain in the field, and suddenly my sheaf rose and stood upright, while your sheaves gathered around and bowed down to mine.”
Gen.37.7.kjv: For, behold, we were binding sheaves in the field, and, lo, my sheaf arose, and also stood upright; and, behold, your sheaves stood round about, and made obeisance to my sheaf.

Gen.37.8.bsb: “Do you intend to reign over us?” his brothers asked. “Will you actually rule us?” So they hated him even more because of his dream and his statements.
Gen.37.8.kjv: And his brethren said to him, Shalt thou indeed reign over us? or shalt thou indeed have dominion over us? And they hated him yet the more for his dreams, and for his words.

Gen.37.9.bsb: Then Joseph had another dream and told it to his brothers. “Look,” he said, “I had another dream, and this time the sun and moon and eleven stars were bowing down to me.”
Gen.37.9.kjv: And he dreamed yet another dream, and told it his brethren, and said, Behold, I have dreamed a dream more; and, behold, the sun and the moon and the eleven stars made obeisance to me.

Gen.37.10.bsb: He told his father and brothers, but his father rebuked him and said, “What is this dream that you have had? Will your mother and brothers and I actually come and bow down to the ground before you?”
Gen.37.10.kjv: And he told it to his father, and to his brethren: and his father rebuked him, and said unto him, What is this dream that thou hast dreamed? Shall I and thy mother and thy brethren indeed come to bow down ourselves to thee to the earth?

Gen.37.11.bsb: And his brothers were jealous of him, but his father kept in mind what he had said.
Gen.37.11.kjv: And his brethren envied him; but his father observed the saying.

Gen.37.19.bsb: “Here comes that dreamer!” they said to one another.
Gen.37.19.kjv: And they said one to another, Behold, this dreamer cometh.

Gen.37.20.bsb: “Come now, let us kill him and throw him into one of the pits. We can say that a vicious animal has devoured him. Then we shall see what becomes of his dreams!”
Gen.37.20.kjv: Come now therefore, and let us slay him, and cast him into some pit, and we will say, Some evil beast hath devoured him: and we shall see what will become of his dreams.

Gen.6.22.bsb: So Noah did everything precisely as God had commanded him.
Gen.6.22.kjv: Thus did Noah; according to all that God commanded him, so did he.

Gen.16.13.bsb: So Hagar gave this name to the LORD who had spoken to her: “You are the God who sees me,” for she said, “Here I have seen the One who sees me!”
Gen.16.13.kjv: And she called the name of the Lord that spake unto her, Thou God seest me: for she said, Have I also here looked after him that seeth me?

Gen.48.21.bsb: Then Israel said to Joseph, “Look, I am about to die, but God will be with you and bring you back to the land of your fathers.
Gen.48.21.kjv: And Israel said unto Joseph, Behold, I die: but God shall be with you, and bring you again unto the land of your fathers.

Gen.50.20.bsb: As for you, what you intended against me for evil, God intended for good, in order to accomplish a day like this—to preserve the lives of many people.
Gen.50.20.kjv: But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.

Gen.6.14.bsb: Make for yourself an ark of gopher wood; make rooms in the ark and coat it with pitch inside and out.
Gen.6.14.kjv: Make thee an ark of gopher wood; rooms shalt thou make in the ark, and shalt pitch it within and without with pitch.

Gen.6.15.bsb: And this is how you are to build it: The ark is to be 300 cubits long, 50 cubits wide, and 30 cubits high.
Gen.6.15.kjv: And this is the fashion which thou shalt make it of: The length of the ark shall be three hundred cubits, the breadth of it fifty cubits, and the height of it thirty cubits.

Gen.6.16.bsb: You are to make a roof for the ark, finish its walls a cubit from the top, place a door in the side of the ark, and build lower, middle, and upper decks.
Gen.6.16.kjv: A window shalt thou make to the ark, and in a cubit shalt thou finish it above; and the door of the ark shalt thou set in the side thereof; with lower, second, and third stories shalt thou make it.

Gen.6.17.bsb: And behold, I will bring floodwaters upon the earth to destroy every creature under the heavens that has the breath of life. Everything on the earth will perish.
Gen.6.17.kjv: And, behold, I, even I, do bring a flood of waters upon the earth, to destroy all flesh, wherein is the breath of life, from under heaven; and every thing that is in the earth shall die.

Gen.6.19.bsb: And you are to bring two of every living creature into the ark—male and female—to keep them alive with you.
Gen.6.19.kjv: And of every living thing of all flesh, two of every sort shalt thou bring into the ark, to keep them alive with thee; they shall be male and female.

Gen.6.20.bsb: Two of every kind of bird and animal and crawling creature will come to you to be kept alive.
Gen.6.20.kjv: Of fowls after their kind, and of cattle after their kind, of every creeping thing of the earth after his kind, two of every sort shall come unto thee, to keep them alive.

Gen.6.21.bsb: You are also to take for yourself every kind of food that is eaten and gather it as food for yourselves and for the animals.”
Gen.6.21.kjv: And take thou unto thee of all food that is eaten, and thou shalt gather it to thee; and it shall be for food for thee, and for them.

Gen.12.4.bsb: So Abram departed, as the LORD had directed him, and Lot went with him. Abram was seventy-five years old when he left Haran.
Gen.12.4.kjv: So Abram departed, as the Lord had spoken unto him; and Lot went with him: and Abram was seventy and five years old when he departed out of Haran.

Gen.15.6.bsb: Abram believed the LORD, and it was credited to him as righteousness.
Gen.15.6.kjv: And he believed in the Lord; and he counted it to him for righteousness.

Gen.15.7.bsb: The LORD also told him, “I am the LORD, who brought you out of Ur of the Chaldeans to give you this land to possess.”
Gen.15.7.kjv: And he said unto him, I am the Lord that brought thee out of Ur of the Chaldees, to give thee this land to inherit it.

Gen.15.8.bsb: But Abram replied, “Lord GOD, how can I know that I will possess it?”
Gen.15.8.kjv: And he said, Lord God, whereby shall I know that I shall inherit it?

Gen.22.1.bsb: Some time later God tested Abraham and said to him, “Abraham!” “Here I am,” he answered.
Gen.22.1.kjv: And it came to pass after these things, that God did tempt Abraham, and said unto him, Abraham: and he said, Behold, here I am.

Gen.22.2.bsb: “Take your son,” God said, “your only son Isaac, whom you love, and go to the land of Moriah. Offer him there as a burnt offering on one of the mountains, which I will show you.”
Gen.22.2.kjv: And he said, Take now thy son, thine only son Isaac, whom thou lovest, and get thee into the land of Moriah; and offer him there for a burnt offering upon one of the mountains which I will tell thee of.

Gen.22.3.bsb: So Abraham got up early the next morning, saddled his donkey, and took along two of his servants and his son Isaac. He split the wood for a burnt offering and set out for the place God had designated.
Gen.22.3.kjv: And Abraham rose up early in the morning, and saddled his ass, and took two of his young men with him, and Isaac his son, and clave the wood for the burnt offering, and rose up, and went unto the place of which God had told him.

Gen.22.4.bsb: On the third day Abraham looked up and saw the place in the distance.
Gen.22.4.kjv: Then on the third day Abraham lifted up his eyes, and saw the place afar off.

Gen.22.5.bsb: “Stay here with the donkey,” Abraham told his servants. “The boy and I will go over there to worship, and then we will return to you.”
Gen.22.5.kjv: And Abraham said unto his young men, Abide ye here with the ass; and I and the lad will go yonder and worship, and come again to you.

Gen.22.19.bsb: Abraham went back to his servants, and they got up and set out together for Beersheba. And Abraham settled in Beersheba.
Gen.22.19.kjv: So Abraham returned unto his young men, and they rose up and went together to Beer–sheba; and Abraham dwelt at Beer–sheba.

Gen.3.13.bsb: Then the LORD God said to the woman, “What is this you have done?” “The serpent deceived me,” she replied, “and I ate.”
Gen.3.13.kjv: And the Lord God said unto the woman, What is this that thou hast done? And the woman said, The serpent beguiled me, and I did eat.

Gen.3.14.bsb: So the LORD God said to the serpent: “Because you have done this, cursed are you above all livestock and every beast of the field! On your belly will you go, and dust you will eat, all the days of your life.
Gen.3.14.kjv: And the Lord God said unto the serpent, Because thou hast done this, thou art cursed above all cattle, and above every beast of the field; upon thy belly shalt thou go, and dust shalt thou eat all the days of thy life:

Gen.45.24.bsb: Then Joseph sent his brothers on their way, and as they were leaving, he said to them, “Do not quarrel on the way!”
Gen.45.24.kjv: So he sent his brethren away, and they departed: and he said unto them, See that ye fall not out by the way.

Gen.50.17.bsb: ‘This is what you are to say to Joseph: I beg you, please forgive the transgression and sin of your brothers, for they did you wrong.’ So now, Joseph, please forgive the transgression of the servants of the God of your father.” When their message came to him, Joseph wept.
Gen.50.17.kjv: So shall ye say unto Joseph, Forgive, I pray thee now, the trespass of thy brethren, and their sin; for they did unto thee evil: and now, we pray thee, forgive the trespass of the servants of the God of thy father. And Joseph wept when they spake unto him.

Gen.50.18.bsb: His brothers also came to him, bowed down before him, and said, “We are your slaves!”
Gen.50.18.kjv: And his brethren also went and fell down before his face; and they said, Behold, we be thy servants.

Gen.50.19.bsb: But Joseph replied, “Do not be afraid. Am I in the place of God?
Gen.50.19.kjv: And Joseph said unto them, Fear not: for am I in the place of God?

Gen.50.21.bsb: Therefore do not be afraid. I will provide for you and your little ones.” So Joseph reassured his brothers and spoke kindly to them.
Gen.50.21.kjv: Now therefore fear ye not: I will nourish you, and your little ones. And he comforted them, and spake kindly unto them.

Gen.27.5.bsb: Now Rebekah was listening to what Isaac told his son Esau. So when Esau went into the field to hunt game and bring it back,
Gen.27.5.kjv: And Rebekah heard when Isaac spake to Esau his son. And Esau went to the field to hunt for venison, and to bring it.

Gen.27.18.bsb: So Jacob went to his father and said, “My father.” “Here I am!” he answered. “Which one are you, my son?”
Gen.27.18.kjv: And he came unto his father, and said, My father: and he said, Here am I; who art thou, my son?

Gen.27.19.bsb: Jacob said to his father, “I am Esau, your firstborn. I have done as you told me. Please sit up and eat some of my game, so that you may bless me.”
Gen.27.19.kjv: And Jacob said unto his father, I am Esau thy firstborn; I have done according as thou badest me: arise, I pray thee, sit and eat of my venison, that thy soul may bless me.

Gen.27.20.bsb: But Isaac asked his son, “How did you ever find it so quickly, my son?” “Because the LORD your God brought it to me,” he replied.
Gen.27.20.kjv: And Isaac said unto his son, How is it that thou hast found it so quickly, my son? And he said, Because the Lord thy God brought it to me.

Gen.27.21.bsb: Then Isaac said to Jacob, “Please come closer so I can touch you, my son. Are you really my son Esau, or not?”
Gen.27.21.kjv: And Isaac said unto Jacob, Come near, I pray thee, that I may feel thee, my son, whether thou be my very son Esau or not.

Gen.27.41.bsb: Esau held a grudge against Jacob because of the blessing his father had given him. And Esau said in his heart, “The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then I will kill my brother Jacob.”
Gen.27.41.kjv: And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing wherewith his father blessed him: and Esau said in his heart, The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then will I slay my brother Jacob.

Gen.27.42.bsb: When the words of her older son Esau were relayed to Rebekah, she sent for her younger son Jacob and told him, “Look, your brother Esau is consoling himself by plotting to kill you.
Gen.27.42.kjv: And these words of Esau her elder son were told to Rebekah: and she sent and called Jacob her younger son, and said unto him, Behold, thy brother Esau, as touching thee, doth comfort himself, purposing to kill thee.

Gen.27.43.bsb: So now, my son, obey my voice and flee at once to my brother Laban in Haran.
Gen.27.43.kjv: Now therefore, my son, obey my voice; and arise, flee thou to Laban my brother to Haran;

Gen.27.44.bsb: Stay with him for a while, until your brother’s fury subsides—
Gen.27.44.kjv: And tarry with him a few days, until thy brother’s fury turn away;

Gen.27.45.bsb: until your brother’s rage against you wanes and he forgets what you have done to him. Then I will send for you and bring you back from there. Why should I lose both of you in one day?”
Gen.27.45.kjv: Until thy brother’s anger turn away from thee, and he forget that which thou hast done to him: then I will send, and fetch thee from thence: why should I be deprived also of you both in one day?

Gen.27.46.bsb: Then Rebekah said to Isaac, “I am weary of my life because of these Hittite women. If Jacob takes a Hittite wife from among them, what good is my life?”
Gen.27.46.kjv: And Rebekah said to Isaac, I am weary of my life because of the daughters of Heth: if Jacob take a wife of the daughters of Heth, such as these which are of the daughters of the land, what good shall my life do me?

Gen.29.31.bsb: When the LORD saw that Leah was unloved, He opened her womb; but Rachel was barren.
Gen.29.31.kjv: And when the Lord saw that Leah was hated, he opened her womb: but Rachel was barren.

Gen.30.3.bsb: Then she said, “Here is my maidservant Bilhah. Sleep with her, that she may bear children for me, so that through her I too can build a family.”
Gen.30.3.kjv: And she said, Behold my maid Bilhah, go in unto her; and she shall bear upon my knees, that I may also have children by her.

Gen.30.4.bsb: So Rachel gave Jacob her servant Bilhah as a wife, and he slept with her,
Gen.30.4.kjv: And she gave him Bilhah her handmaid to wife: and Jacob went in unto her.

Gen.30.5.bsb: and Bilhah conceived and bore him a son.
Gen.30.5.kjv: And Bilhah conceived, and bare Jacob a son.

Gen.30.7.bsb: And Rachel’s servant Bilhah conceived again and bore Jacob a second son.
Gen.30.7.kjv: And Bilhah Rachel’s maid conceived again, and bare Jacob a second son.

Gen.30.8.bsb: Then Rachel said, “In my great struggles, I have wrestled with my sister and won.” So she named him Naphtali.
Gen.30.8.kjv: And Rachel said, With great wrestlings have I wrestled with my sister, and I have prevailed: and she called his name Naphtali.

Gen.30.9.bsb: When Leah saw that she had stopped having children, she gave her servant Zilpah to Jacob as a wife.
Gen.30.9.kjv: When Leah saw that she had left bearing, she took Zilpah her maid, and gave her Jacob to wife.

Gen.30.10.bsb: And Leah’s servant Zilpah bore Jacob a son.
Gen.30.10.kjv: And Zilpah Leah’s maid bare Jacob a son.

Gen.30.11.bsb: Then Leah said, “How fortunate!” So she named him Gad.
Gen.30.11.kjv: And Leah said, A troop cometh: and she called his name Gad.

Gen.30.12.bsb: When Leah’s servant Zilpah bore Jacob a second son,
Gen.30.12.kjv: And Zilpah Leah’s maid bare Jacob a second son.

Gen.30.13.bsb: Leah said, “How happy I am! For the women call me happy.” So she named him Asher.
Gen.30.13.kjv: And Leah said, Happy am I, for the daughters will call me blessed: and she called his name Asher.

Gen.30.14.bsb: Now during the wheat harvest, Reuben went out and found some mandrakes in the field. When he brought them to his mother, Rachel begged Leah, “Please give me some of your son’s mandrakes.”
Gen.30.14.kjv: And Reuben went in the days of wheat harvest, and found mandrakes in the field, and brought them unto his mother Leah. Then Rachel said to Leah, Give me, I pray thee, of thy son’s mandrakes.

Gen.30.16.bsb: When Jacob came in from the field that evening, Leah went out to meet him and said, “You must come with me, for I have hired you with my son’s mandrakes.” So he slept with her that night.
Gen.30.16.kjv: And Jacob came out of the field in the evening, and Leah went out to meet him, and said, Thou must come in unto me; for surely I have hired thee with my son’s mandrakes. And he lay with her that night.

Gen.30.25.bsb: Now after Rachel had given birth to Joseph, Jacob said to Laban, “Send me on my way so I can return to my homeland.
Gen.30.25.kjv: And it came to pass, when Rachel had born Joseph, that Jacob said unto Laban, Send me away, that I may go unto mine own place, and to my country.

Gen.13.3.bsb: From the Negev he journeyed from place to place toward Bethel, until he came to the place between Bethel and Ai where his tent had formerly been pitched,
Gen.13.3.kjv: And he went on his journeys from the south even to Beth–el, unto the place where his tent had been at the beginning, between Beth–el and Hai;

Gen.13.4.bsb: to the site where he had built the altar. And there Abram called on the name of the LORD.
Gen.13.4.kjv: Unto the place of the altar, which he had made there at the first: and there Abram called on the name of the Lord.

Gen.3.20.bsb: And Adam named his wife Eve, because she would be the mother of all the living.
Gen.3.20.kjv: And Adam called his wife’s name Eve; because she was the mother of all living.

Gen.18.3.bsb: “My lord,” said Abraham, “if I have found favor in your sight, please do not pass your servant by.
Gen.18.3.kjv: And said, My Lord, if now I have found favour in thy sight, pass not away, I pray thee, from thy servant:

Gen.18.4.bsb: Let a little water be brought, that you may wash your feet and rest yourselves under the tree.
Gen.18.4.kjv: Let a little water, I pray you, be fetched, and wash your feet, and rest yourselves under the tree:

Gen.18.5.bsb: And I will bring a bit of bread so that you may refresh yourselves. This is why you have passed your servant’s way. After that, you may continue on your way.” “Yes,” they replied, “you may do as you have said.”
Gen.18.5.kjv: And I will fetch a morsel of bread, and comfort ye your hearts; after that ye shall pass on: for therefore are ye come to your servant. And they said, So do, as thou hast said.

Gen.18.7.bsb: Meanwhile, Abraham ran to the herd, selected a tender and choice calf, and gave it to a servant, who hurried to prepare it.
Gen.18.7.kjv: And Abraham ran unto the herd, and fetcht a calf tender and good, and gave it unto a young man; and he hasted to dress it.

Gen.18.8.bsb: Then Abraham brought curds and milk and the calf that had been prepared, and he set them before the men and stood by them under the tree as they ate.
Gen.18.8.kjv: And he took butter, and milk, and the calf which he had dressed, and set it before them; and he stood by them under the tree, and they did eat.

Gen.18.10.bsb: Then the LORD said, “I will surely return to you at this time next year, and your wife Sarah will have a son!” Now Sarah was behind him, listening at the entrance to the tent.
Gen.18.10.kjv: And he said, I will certainly return unto thee according to the time of life; and, lo, Sarah thy wife shall have a son. And Sarah heard it in the tent door, which was behind him.

Gen.18.11.bsb: And Abraham and Sarah were already old and well along in years; Sarah had passed the age of childbearing.
Gen.18.11.kjv: Now Abraham and Sarah were old and well stricken in age; and it ceased to be with Sarah after the manner of women.

Gen.18.13.bsb: And the LORD asked Abraham, “Why did Sarah laugh and say, ‘Can I really bear a child when I am old?’
Gen.18.13.kjv: And the Lord said unto Abraham, Wherefore did Sarah laugh, saying, Shall I of a surety bear a child, which am old?

Gen.18.14.bsb: Is anything too difficult for the LORD? At the appointed time I will return to you—in about a year—and Sarah will have a son.”
Gen.18.14.kjv: Is any thing too hard for the Lord? At the time appointed I will return unto thee, according to the time of life, and Sarah shall have a son.

Gen.18.15.bsb: But Sarah was afraid, so she denied it and said, “I did not laugh.” “No,” replied the LORD, “but you did laugh.”
Gen.18.15.kjv: Then Sarah denied, saying, I laughed not; for she was afraid. And he said, Nay; but thou didst laugh.

Gen.18.16.bsb: When the men got up to leave, they looked out over Sodom, and Abraham walked along with them to see them off.
Gen.18.16.kjv: And the men rose up from thence, and looked toward Sodom: and Abraham went with them to bring them on the way.

Gen.18.20.bsb: Then the LORD said, “The outcry against Sodom and Gomorrah is great. Because their sin is so grievous,
Gen.18.20.kjv: And the Lord said, Because the cry of Sodom and Gomorrah is great, and because their sin is very grievous;

Gen.18.22.bsb: And the two men turned away and went toward Sodom, but Abraham remained standing before the LORD.
Gen.18.22.kjv: And the men turned their faces from thence, and went toward Sodom: but Abraham stood yet before the Lord.

Gen.35.9.bsb: After Jacob had returned from Paddan-aram, God appeared to him again and blessed him.
Gen.35.9.kjv: And God appeared unto Jacob again, when he came out of Padan–aram, and blessed him.

Gen.1.2.bsb: Now the earth was formless and void, and darkness was over the surface of the deep. And the Spirit of God was hovering over the surface of the waters.
Gen.1.2.kjv: And the earth was without form and void; and darkness was upon the face of the deep. And the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters.

Gen.1.25.bsb: God made the beasts of the earth according to their kinds, the livestock according to their kinds, and everything that crawls upon the earth according to its kind. And God saw that it was good.
Gen.1.25.kjv: And God made the beast of the earth after his kind, and cattle after their kind, and every thing that creepeth upon the earth after his kind: and God saw that it was good.

Gen.2.6.bsb: But springs welled up from the earth and watered the whole surface of the ground.
Gen.2.6.kjv: But there went up a mist from the earth, and watered the whole face of the ground.

Gen.2.8.bsb: And the LORD God planted a garden in Eden, in the east, where He placed the man He had formed.
Gen.2.8.kjv: And the Lord God planted a garden eastward in Eden; and there he put the man whom he had formed.

Gen.2.9.bsb: Out of the ground the LORD God gave growth to every tree that is pleasing to the eye and good for food. And in the middle of the garden were the tree of life and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
Gen.2.9.kjv: And out of the ground made the Lord God to grow every tree that is pleasant to the sight and good for food; the tree of life also in the midst of the garden, and the tree of knowledge of good and evil.

Gen.2.10.bsb: Now a river flowed out of Eden to water the garden, and from there it branched into four headwaters:
Gen.2.10.kjv: And a river went out of Eden to water the garden; and from thence it was parted, and became into four heads.

Gen.2.11.bsb: The name of the first river is the Pishon; it winds through the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold.
Gen.2.11.kjv: The name of the first is Pison: that is it which compasseth the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold;

Gen.2.12.bsb: And the gold of that land is pure, and bdellium and onyx are found there.
Gen.2.12.kjv: And the gold of that land is good: there is bdellium and the onyx stone.

Gen.2.13.bsb: The name of the second river is the Gihon; it winds through the whole land of Cush.
Gen.2.13.kjv: And the name of the second river is Gihon: the same is it that compasseth the whole land of Ethiopia.

Gen.2.14.bsb: The name of the third river is the Tigris; it runs along the east side of Assyria. And the fourth river is the Euphrates.
Gen.2.14.kjv: And the name of the third river is Hiddekel: that is it which goeth toward the east of Assyria. And the fourth river is Euphrates.

Gen.21.33.bsb: And Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Beersheba, and there he called upon the name of the LORD, the Eternal God.
Gen.21.33.kjv: And Abraham planted a grove in Beer–sheba, and called there on the name of the Lord, the everlasting God.

Gen.6.8.bsb: Noah, however, found favor in the eyes of the LORD.
Gen.6.8.kjv: But Noah found grace in the eyes of the Lord.

Gen.6.9.bsb: This is the account of Noah. Noah was a righteous man, blameless in his generation; Noah walked with God.
Gen.6.9.kjv: These are the generations of Noah: Noah was a just man and perfect in his generations, and Noah walked with God.

Gen.46.4.bsb: I will go down with you to Egypt, and I will surely bring you back. And Joseph’s own hands will close your eyes.”
Gen.46.4.kjv: I will go down with thee into Egypt; and I will also surely bring thee up again: and Joseph shall put his hand upon thine eyes.

Gen.20.6.bsb: Then God said to Abimelech in the dream, “Yes, I know that you did this with a clear conscience, and so I have kept you from sinning against Me. That is why I did not let you touch her.
Gen.20.6.kjv: And God said unto him in a dream, Yea, I know that thou didst this in the integrity of thy heart; for I also withheld thee from sinning against me: therefore suffered I thee not to touch her.

Gen.6.3.bsb: So the LORD said, “My Spirit will not contend with man forever, for he is mortal; his days shall be 120 years.”
Gen.6.3.kjv: And the Lord said, My spirit shall not always strive with man, for that he also is flesh: yet his days shall be an hundred and twenty years.

Gen.46.3.bsb: “I am God,” He said, “the God of your father. Do not be afraid to go down to Egypt, for I will make you into a great nation there.
Gen.46.3.kjv: And he said, I am God, the God of thy father: fear not to go down into Egypt; for I will there make of thee a great nation:

Gen.28.16.bsb: When Jacob woke up, he said, “Surely the LORD is in this place, and I was unaware of it.”
Gen.28.16.kjv: And Jacob awaked out of his sleep, and he said, Surely the Lord is in this place; and I knew it not.

Gen.31.3.bsb: Then the LORD said to Jacob, “Go back to the land of your fathers and to your kindred, and I will be with you.”
Gen.31.3.kjv: And the Lord said unto Jacob, Return unto the land of thy fathers, and to thy kindred; and I will be with thee.

Gen.48.15.bsb: Then he blessed Joseph and said: “May the God before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac walked, the God who has been my shepherd all my life to this day,
Gen.48.15.kjv: And he blessed Joseph, and said, God, before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac did walk, the God which fed me all my life long unto this day,
